datasets.title: Mobile data basket (5 GB minimum)

The 5 GB mobile basket must not be spliced into the older 2 GB series. Connection charges and device costs are not added to this monthly figure.

Rated capacity is not actual electricity consumption or AI-specific compute.

datasets.title: GDP per capita — latest available
datasets.description: Gross domestic product is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. It can be measured in three different ways: using either the expenditure approach, the income approach, or the production approach. The core indicator has been divided by the general population to achieve a per capita estimate.This indicator is expressed in current prices, meaning no adjustment has been made to account for price changes over time. This indicator is expressed in United States dollars. One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

datasets.title: Manufacturing value added — latest available
datasets.description: Manufacturing includes industries classified in ISIC (Rev. 3) major division C and is defined as the physical or chemical transformation of materials or components into new products. Value added is the contribution to the economy by a producer or an industry or an institutional sector, which is estimated by the total value of output produced and deducting the total value of intermediate consumption of goods and services used to produce that output. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

datasets.title: Labour productivity — latest available
datasets.unit: GDP per person employed, constant 2021 PPP $
datasets.description: GDP per person employed is gross domestic product (GDP) divided by total employment in the economy. Purchasing power parity (PPP) GDP is GDP converted to 2021 constant international dollars using PPP rates. An international dollar has the same purchasing power over GDP that a U.S. dollar has in the United States. One current WDI vintage across all years. Historical values may be revised. Do not splice with older vintages; see the source definition for method changes.

datasets.title: Eskom Homelight 20A electricity rate — latest available
datasets.description: Published flat active-energy charge for Eskom direct Homelight 20A customers in South Africa, VAT included. Cents per kWh divided by 100 to obtain ZAR/kWh. Not a national average, municipal resale, industrial tariff or modelled household bill. Applicable tariff years start on 1 April. Flat-rate structure introduced in April 2025. Earlier inclining-block prices are incompatible and not joined. No foreign-exchange conversion. Rate validity ends 31 March of the next year; subsequent tariff changes need a new source review.

projects.definition: Colocation and hyperscale data centre facilities of 1 MW design capacity or above, plus nationally announced cloud or AI compute programmes, publicly announced and traceable to a named source. Enterprise self-build, sub-1 MW sites and unannounced facilities are out of scope in this version. The definition is published so coverage can be judged against it, and it will be revised in the open.
projects.unit: MW (capacity) and USD (capital). The two are never summed.

status_key.under_construction: Building, with a stated target date
status_key.approved: Planning consent or licence granted; not yet building
status_key.announced: Publicly announced by a sponsor or government; no consent evidence yet
status_key.exploring: Discussions or bidding reported; nothing committed
status_key.funding: Capital raised for a portfolio, not a single site
status_key.appeal_pending: Planning approval suspended while an appeal is decided; not construction

universe.note: Reference figures are published by others and are not our own count. They are recorded so coverage can be stated honestly rather than implied.
universe.facilities_estimate: 223-230 operational facilities across 38 countries (competing estimates; definitions differ)
universe.facilities_tracked_range: one portfolio database counts 125 existing and 46 upcoming colocation sites

sources.name: African Data Centres Association, Data Centres in Africa 2026
Nairametrics, Top 15 African countries with the most data centres

projects.name: Nairobi Two (NBO2)
projects.note: Opened on 7 September 2026; iColo sites rebranded to Digital Realty across Kenya and Mozambique.

projects.name: KASI hyperscale campus (NSIA investment)
projects.note: The 100 MW is the long-term full-campus design, not capacity already serving load. NSIA reported the LOS1 flag-off on 19 May 2026, followed by phased commissioning, systems integration and customer readiness. No separately quantified operational IT load was published in this source; the 100 MW remains planned.

projects.name: MTN AI-ready data centres
projects.note: About 150 MW is the reported initial capacity across Nigeria and South Africa; the national split is not published, so it is not assigned to either country.

projects.name: Vodafone, Elsewedy and Cassava data centre
projects.note: Capacity undisclosed, so the MW field is left empty rather than estimated.

projects.name: Hassan Allam data centres (first phase)
projects.note: Licensed with a stated first-phase investment.

projects.name: Heka Data AI hub
projects.note: Exploratory; recorded so the pipeline is visible, not counted as capacity.

projects.name: Huawei AI data centre bid
projects.note: Reported to have prompted a US counteroffer; geopolitically significant, commercially uncommitted.

projects.name: Airtel Kenya data centre
projects.note: Airtel half-year results published 30 October 2026, page 11, confirm construction continues in Kenya and Nigeria. July 2027 completion is the later reported target; older operator/government pages still say Q1 2027. The reported 44 MW design is not added to comparable IT-load totals because its basis is unconfirmed.
projects.capacity_basis: 44 MW reported design capacity; not confirmed as critical IT load, excluded from capacity_mw

projects.name: Mombasa AI data centre
projects.note: Reported in shillings; not converted here, because the exchange rate on the day of reporting is part of the record. The shilling figure covers the smart power system intended to energise the data centre, with GE Vernova supplying gas turbines, not the data centre's entire capital cost. Reported in shillings; not converted here.

projects.name: Equinix King Air Industria campus (two sites)
projects.note: No confirmed IT capacity is published. The earlier 174 MW figure described electricity demand, not installed or declared IT capacity; the July land-use approval was legally suspended after an appeal, and Equinix reported no immediate development plans (20 September 2026). The August approval report and September appeal concern the same King Air Industria campus; merged to prevent duplicate project counts. Latest reviewed reporting still describes approval suspended pending appeal, not construction.
projects.status_detail: Planning approval legally suspended pending appeal; no immediate development plan reported.

projects.name: Teraco JB7 data centre expansion
projects.note: Teraco announced construction on 13 November 2024: 40 MW critical IT load, with completion scheduled for 2026. No commissioning confirmation located in this review. Portfolio totals are excluded from this project capacity.
projects.status_detail: MyBroadband reported it was still expanding on 27 August 2026; the 2026 completion date is a schedule, not confirmation of commissioning.

projects.name: Cassava AI Factory
projects.note: Ranked 36th on the TOP500 supercomputer list; 12,000-GPU buildout reported at US$700m.

projects.name: Raxio expansion programme
projects.note: Raxio reported more than US$380 million in committed company capital, including shareholder equity and prior financing. No site-specific capex or capacity is stated; this amount is not treated as project capex.
projects.status_detail: Portfolio-level committed capital, not project capex.

projects.name: Africa Data Centres Accra
projects.note: The operator announced an initial 10 MW design, expandable to 30 MW depending on demand, with first-phase completion then expected within 12 months. No later public commissioning update was located by 26 September 2026; operational status is therefore unknown.
projects.status_detail: 2023 plan; current commissioning or construction status not confirmed in reviewed sources.

projects.name: Wiocc capital raise
projects.note: Cable and connectivity capital, recorded separately from data centre capacity.

projects.name: Côte d'Ivoire sovereign data centre
projects.note: Sovereign national data-centre programme reported approved in July 2026. Financing covers a broader government digitisation and smart-border package; no site-specific MW or capex is assigned. Broken truncated source link replaced with the full article.

projects.name: Gabon sovereign data centre
projects.note: Launched with capacity undisclosed.

projects.name: Cybastion AI hub
projects.note: Anchors a national AI hub programme.

projects.name: Nigeria cloud and AI investment target
projects.source: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy
projects.note: The National Digital Cloud Policy sets a government ambition to mobilise US$250 million in private investment in 12 months and US$750 million within 24 months. These are targets, not committed spend or installed capacity.
projects.originating_source: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation & Digital Economy
projects.status_detail: Government mobilization target, not committed capital or project capex.

projects.name: Project BRIDGE fibre programme
projects.note: 90,000 km of new fibre in execution phase; connectivity, counted separately from compute.

projects.name: Nexus AI factory (Casablanca)
projects.sponsors: Nexus Core Systems; Moroccan government partners
projects.note: Planned capacity; USD 1.2 billion is the initial investment announcement. No commissioning evidence. Announcement month only.

facilities.name: Angola National Data Centre (INFOSI)
facilities.operator: INFOSI (National Institute for Promotion of Information Society)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Under construction as of Nov 2025 (75% complete). Expected operational H1 2026. Modular design: 12 containers x 28 racks = 336 racks total. Part of $90M combined investment including unified government cloud. All government services to migrate within 30 days of inauguration. Director General Andre Pedro (INFOSI) confirmed status Nov 2025. FurtherAfrica (Feb 2023) placed the main data centre on a 5,320 m² site in Camama, Luanda, with a backup at the existing National Data Centre in Rangel. Status=2 (Under construction).. [MINTTICS Portal](https://consultapublica.minttics.gov.ao), [Wikipedia Angola Telecom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angola_Telecom), [FurtherAfrica National Cloud](https://furtherafrica.com/2023/02/22/angola-invests-us89m-in-national-cloud-project/), [Ecofin National DC](https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/1411-50505-angola-nears-completion-of-national-data-center-set-for-2026-launch), [Raxio DC](https://www.raxiogroup.com/raxio-opens-angolas-largest-data-centre-in-landmark-30-million-expansion/) (private, separate), [DTRI Angola](https://dtri.uneca.org/v1/uploads/country-profile/ago-country-profile-en.pdf) Inaugurated 28 April 2026 by President João Lourenço between Camama and Kilamba; built in about 10 months; designed to Uptime Tier III (design standard, no certification stated). 208 racks installed in 12 container modules of 28 (336 capacity). 1,040 kW is the power capacity as reported, not stated to be IT load. Floor space 6,225 m² is the site area. $89M (Angop, April 2026) is the same national-cloud budget MINTTICS gave in February 2023 for both data centres and training. ANGOSAT-2 provides satellite redundancy (GGPEN, May 2026); the INFOSI backup centre replicates it in real time since August 2026. Inaugurated at the end of April 2026, an $89m project occupying 6,225 m2, not stated whether building or campus (ITWeb, 15 June 2026). Inaugurated by the President on 28 April 2026 at Camama (Angop, PTI, 28 April 2026); Angop gives 208 racks and 1,040 kW at inauguration against the 336-rack design. The 12 modules were certified Tier III by Uptime in Presight's name, but the building had no Uptime certification as of June 2026, INFOSI awaiting an audit (Expansão, 1 June 2026); Angop's 1,040 kW is not stated as IT load.

Exact per-facility split unknown.. [Data Center Dynamics](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/govt-of-burkina-faso-launches-two-mini-data-centers-to-support-data-sovereignty/), [leFaso.net](https://lefaso.net/spip.php?article143948), [Developing Telecoms](https://developingtelecoms.com/telecom-technology/data-centres-networks/19660-burkina-faso-launches-two-mini-data-centres-in-data-sovereignty-push.html), [Pulse of Africa](https://pulseofafrica.info/innovation/154), Burkina Faso Ministry of Digital Transition Facebook post The cost is in West African CFA francs (XOF), not XAF: TechAfrica News and Connecting Africa give an estimated 16bn FCFA (US$28.9m, Jan 2026); the minister said over 15bn FCFA (Sidwaya, 25 Jan 2026); the Primature's own statement gives no figures. Status per the 25 Jul 2026 mid-year review: 120 platforms hosted abroad are being moved to the two centres by end-2026 (Queen Mafa). Telecompaper (25 Aug 2025) reports Cybastion signed a deal to bring a modular data centre of 10-40 racks (5-8 kW per rack) by road to Ouagadougou; whether it is one of these two is not stated. Lefaso put the build at FCFA 15.2bn with about FCFA 500m of running costs over three years, and five to ten days of backup power per site. The digital-transition minister put the cost of the two modular data centres at FCFA 15bn at a public accountability review on 8 October 2026, against the FCFA 16bn stated at inauguration, and said they had multiplied the hosting capacity previously available by ten; the national data centre still to come was put at an estimated FCFA 20bn, with no site or capacity stated.

[Company Website](https://greenline-tech.com), [ZoomInfo](https://www.zoominfo.com/c/greenline-technologies-inc/357422442), [LinkedIn CEO](https://www.linkedin.com/in/alexandru-postelnicu-95a5438), [SOCATEL News](https://greenline-tech.com/news/Greenline-Technologies-Awarded-Landmark-Privatization-of-SOCATEL-in-the-Central-African-Republic), [Parakou News](https://greenline-tech.com/news/greenline-technologies-signs-definitive-agreements-for-the-grand-parakou-project-in-benin) On 16 July 2026 the government and Greenline launched implementation of the MoU, restating US$150 million for network modernisation and a Tier 3 data centre; definitive takeover agreements, a joint steering committee and a deployment schedule were still to be agreed, and the split of ownership and financing was undisclosed (Agence Ecofin, 17 July 2026). facilities.name: Equinix AB1 (formerly MDXi/MainOne Abidjan)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

ABJ1.2 (new Tier III facility) added Nov 2023 at same VITIB site. PeeringDB GPS shared with Raxio at VITIB. Networks at facility: AS37282 (MainOne/Equinix), AS328840 (ST Digital), AS36924 (GVA). [Equinix Investor](https://investor.equinix.com), [Yahoo Finance Holders](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/EQIX/holders/), [MainOne Acquisition PR](https://newsroom.equinix.com/2022-04-05-Equinix-Enters-Africa,-Closing-the-US-320-Million-Acquisition-of-MainOne), [DCD News](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com)

facilities.name: PAIX Abidjan ABJ-1
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Located Bonoumin, Cocody CBD, Abidjan. GPS approximate for Bonoumin quarter. 2000 kW IT load; 240 cabinets; 900 sqm colo space. 2N UPS; N+1 generators; N+1 cooling redundancy. CIVIX/CI-IX internet exchange on-site per PAIX website. Access to 20+ carriers and ISPs. PAIX HQ Amsterdam, NLD. [Africa50 PAIX](https://www.africa50.com/our-funds/projects/paix-data-centers/), [PAIX Investors](https://www.paix.io/investors), [Africa50 Governance](https://www.africa50.com/our-company/structure-governance/), [Africa50 News](https://www.africa50.com/media/news/article/paix-data-centres-expands-capacity-in-ghana-to-12-mw/) Status per Invest International's project disclosure (November 2024): a EUR 300,000 development contribution to PAIX Indigo B.V. for the feasibility study and ESIA of a data centre in Côte d'Ivoire. The specifications above are PAIX's advertised design, not a built facility.

facilities.name: Raxio CIV1
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Inaugurated Sep 24 2024. First Uptime Institute Tier III certified carrier-neutral DC in CIV. VITIB Zone Franche Grand Bassam; Bloc A Ilot 8 Lot 1 Parc Technologique Mahatma Gandhi. GPS from PeeringDB. Initial 400 racks; full build 800 racks at 3MW. 2,000 m2 is white space. Seven layers physical security. MoU with Ministry of Digital Transition Jun 2025 for govt services hosting. Roha Group (US) + Meridiam (France) own Raxio; [Raxio Group site](https://www.raxiogroup.com), [Roha Group](https://www.roha-africa.com), [Meridiam](https://www.meridiam.com), [IFC disclosure](https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/AS-ESRS/48537/raxio-dc), [Raxio $46M equity PR](https://www.raxiogroup.com/raxio-data-centres-raises-additional-46-million-in-equity-funding-bolstering-its-position-as-africas-best-funded-data-centre-platform-and-announces-ceo-succession-plan/), [Meridiam investment PR](https://www.meridiam.com/news/raxio-data-centres/) The October 2022 environmental study describes a 2,790 m2 building on a 1.2 ha plot, with about 400 racks and 1.5 MW of IT power in the first phase.

facilities.name: Orange GOS Data Centre Grand Bassam
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Built 2016 Grand Bassam Free Zone; site 16600 sqm; building 1450 sqm, of which computer room 420 sqm; power capacity 1.3MW (not stated as IT load). Uptime Institute Tier III design cert confirmed. Solar plant 355 kWp (781 panels) commissioned Oct 2022 (begun with Engie, completed by Butec); renewable energy ~48% (solar + CIE hydro). Primarily Orange OMEA subsidiaries but offers BtoB colocation. Orange parent HQ France; PUE 1.8 estimated. Hybrid cooling (CRAC + solar-assisted).. [[Orange Annual Report 2024-25](https://rai.orange.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/54/2025/06/integrated-annual-report-2024-2025.pdf), [MarketScreener Shareholders](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/ORANGE-S-A-78824405/company-shareholders/), [Simply Wall St Ownership](https://simplywall.st/stocks/it/telecom/bit-1ora/orange-shares/ownership), [Orange Board](https://www.orange.com/en/our-group/our-governance/our-board-of-directors), [IFC Orange Mali](https://www.ifc.org/en/pressroom/2025/ifc-invests-in-orange-mali-to-expand-digital-connectivity-and-support-women-s-digi), [AWS Partnership](https://www.orange.com/en/press-release/orange-middle-east-amp-africa-and-amazon-web-services-collaborate-to-bring-advanced-cloud-technologies-to-customers-in-north-and-west-africa-233909)] Cloudoor launched its Door sovereign cloud with GOS in March 2025 (a Linfodrome advertorial).

Dual-purpose switching and colocation. MTN Group HQ Fairlands South Africa. No Uptime tier cert found. GPS approximate Yopougon district.. [MTN FY24 AFS](https://www.mtn.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/MTN-Group-FY-24-Annual-Financial-Statements.pdf), [Simply Wall St](https://simplywall.st/), [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MTN_Group), [MTN.com](https://www.mtn.com/) Abidjan.net (6 June 2014) confirms this row's facility: the Flexenclosure eCentre in the Yopougon industrial zone, 336 m² on a 2,000 m² plot, over FCFA 1bn, inaugurated 5 June 2014. MTN's other Abidjan sites (the 2011 Technology Center in Zone 4, and the site on Bd François Mitterrand that DataCenterMap lists) have their own rows.

facilities.name: SNDI Government Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: SNDI is state-owned IT agency for GoCI government. DC operational since at least 2012; supports all ministries via nationwide WAN (VSAT-based + fibre). Server virtualisation deployed. No public specs on capacity floor space or tier. Cybernetica signed contract Sep 2025 to deploy secure data exchange layer (UXP). GPS approximate Abidjan Plateau government district. Sovereign domestic ownership; [Telecom.gouv.ci (Official Ministry Site)](https://www.telecom.gouv.ci), [Trade.gov Côte d'Ivoire Digital Economy](https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/cote-divoire-digital-economy), [Cybastion National Data Center](https://www.cybastiontech.com/ivorian-minister-of-digital-transition-and-digitalization-visits-cybastion-led-national-data-center-construction-site/), [Raxio Côte d'Ivoire](https://www.raxiogroup.com/data-centres/cote-divoire/) An African Development Bank appraisal (June 2023) rates SNDI's data centre Tier 2-type and says the administration's site at SNDI is the only government data centre with a backup site. The PARAE project document (June 2023, reported by Sika Finance in September 2026) counts SNDI's among the four operational state data centres, calls their equipment obsolete, and says the administration's centre hosted at SNDI is the only one with a backup site.

facilities.name: National Data Centre Cote d'Ivoire (Digital City Grand Bassam)
facilities.operator: ANSUT (Agence Nationale du Service Universel des Télécommunications/TIC); built by Cybastion Institute of Technology LLC
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: First stone Dec 14 2023 at AIGF Marcory-Anoumabo; civil works restarted May 2025 at VITIB Grand Bassam (Digital City). $60m budget ($66m US EXIM Bank loan guarantee). Tier III design, 20000 sqm site. Cybastion (US firm) main contractor; Cisco equipment training Dec 2025. ~20% complete as of Dec 2025. IT load 1MW from D4D pipeline data. [EXIM $66M](https://www.exim.gov/news/export-import-bank-united-states-board-directors-approves-nearly-514-million-strengthen), [EXIM $47M](https://www.exim.gov/news/export-import-bank-united-states-board-directors-approves-nearly-47-million-transaction-cote), [Ministry Visit](https://telecom.gouv.ci/new/actualite/73), [CIO Mag DCs](https://cio-mag.com/cote-divoire-un-nouveau-datacenter-construit-en-huit-mois-un-exploit-mondial-affirme-steve-tchouaga/), [Financial Afrik](https://www.financialafrik.com/en/2025/08/28/ivory-coast-66-million-funding-for-the-first-national-data-center/) DCD (9 September 2026): opening planned for 2027, 1.73 MW IT within 3 MW total power, 228 racks, 10 PB storage, estimated cost $66M, offering cloud hosting, colocation and connectivity to government bodies; this replaces the 1 MW and 2 x 400 racks announced in December 2023. AIP (9 December 2025) gave financing of FCFA 42.361bn, delivery at end-2026 and BNETD as engineer. EXIM's board approved on 21 August 2025 a $66,138,119 guarantee to Citibank N.A., borrower the Ministry of Finance and Budget, end user the Ministry of Digital Transition. CIO Africa (September 2026) names Cisco, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Schneider Electric among Cybastion's technology partners on the build.

facilities.name: ST Digital Grand Bassam (STD Abidjan)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Inaugurated Oct 2 2025 at VITIB II Grand Bassam. 4000 sqm (CIO Mag gives it as the site area); 3 modules; 160 racks (42U each); 6000+ physical servers; 50000+ virtual servers. Tier III design. OVHcloud partnership for sovereign cloud. Eco-responsible design (vegetable gardens; artificial lakes reusing AC output). Exclusively African-designed/operated. UHURU Investment Partners invested EUR 10m in ST Digital before the build (DCD). Hybrid cooling (CRAC + evaporative water reuse).. [ST Digital](https://st.digital), [DCD Côte d'Ivoire](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/st-digital-starts-construction-on-data-center-in-cote-divoire/), [Business in Cameroon](https://www.businessincameroon.com/public-management/2506-14789-cameroon-s-st-digital-ranks-among-africa-s-leading-digital-investors-says-unctad), [Uhuru](https://www.uhuruinvestment.com), [IFC Uhuru](https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/46119/uhuru-growth-fund-i), [US DFC Uhuru](https://www.dfc.gov/sites/default/files/media/documents/BDR(22)25_UhuruInvestmentPartners_0.pdf)

facilities.name: STD Douala (DLA01)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: First carrier-neutral Tier III data centre in Central Africa. DC OIX-2 + IXP OIX-1 certified (Open-IX). Houses DOUALA-IX IXP. Peering at CAMIX NAP. Tier III compliant (not Uptime-certified). Domestic private (CMR). renewable_energy_pct~63 per Cameroon grid average.. [DCD on CI DC](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/st-digital-starts-construction-on-data-center-in-cote-divoire/), [TechCabal on expansion](https://techcabal.com/2024/05/17/st-digital-to-build-additional-data-centres-in-3-francophone-countries/), [ST Digital site](https://st.digital), [Uhuru on Preqin](https://www.preqin.com/data/profile/fund-manager/uhuru-investment-partners/216011), [Businessday on Uhuru backers](https://businessday.ng/news/article/nigeria-based-pe-firm-uhuru-raises-n113m/), [LinkedIn Anthony Same](https://www.linkedin.com/in/anthonysame) MINPOSTEL (14 July 2025) places the site in Douala's port zone. CAMIX (7 April 2026) hosts its third PoP here, in a carrier-hotel setting, in service since 1 July (year not stated), with INK and ST Digital connected. ST Digital launched its Douala Cloud & Datacenter Services on 22 January 2021 (Douala Today, 26 January 2021; EcoMatin, 28 January 2021). PeeringDB gives the address Immeuble SCI Chimede, Rue 1033, port de Douala, Bonanjo. ST Digital's OCP Ready self-assessment (completed January 2024) gives 500 m2 of white space (the floor-space figure), 1 MW of critical IT power, two utility feeds, three generators, racks up to 12 kW and a design PUE under 1.5, and names Orange, MTN, Camtel and others as network providers.

facilities.name: Raxio DRC1
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

[IFC Disclosure](https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/48537/raxio-dc), [IFC Project PDF](https://ewsdata.rightsindevelopment.org/projects/IFC-48537/pdf/), [Raxio About](https://www.raxiogroup.com/about-raxio/), [Meridiam Raxio](https://www.meridiam.com/assets/raxio-data-centres/), [Raxio Press IFC](https://www.raxiogroup.com/raxio-secures-100-million-from-ifc-to-develop-leading-sub-saharan-african-data-center-platform/), [Raxio Debt](https://www.raxiogroup.com/raxio-data-centres-raises-up-to-170m-sustainability-linked-debt-facility-to-accelerate-digital-transformation-in-africa/) KINIX, the ISPA-DRC exchange, relocated its IXP infrastructure into DRC1 (Raxio, 20 August 2026). Built by MBTP SA (ACTUALITE.CD, October 2025).

facilities.name: OADC Texaf Digital Kinshasa
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: DRC first live Uptime Tier-III DC (OADC's claim; Raxio makes the same claim for DRC1). 2MW 550+ racks; 1,500 m² is IT white space (CIO Africa). Triple certified ISO 27001+22301+PCI DSS (Feb 2025). SNEL hydro utility ~95% renewable. Low PUE. OADC GBR/Texaf-backed. ST Digital CMR partnership. Hosts ACIX peering.. [Research summary](workspace://wiocc_kenya_oadc_research.md) [wiocc.net](https://wiocc.net) [IFC disclosures](https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/SII/38381/wiocc-investment) ACIX (operated by DE-CIX for Internet pour Tous) added a node at the facility, which OADC calls FIH1 (ITWeb, 19 May 2026). Public peering records list KINIX at the facility as well as at Raxio DRC1, making KINIX a two-site exchange (Tech Africa, 21 August 2026).

facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source

[Credence Data GBS SARL](https://www.credencedata.com/company-profile/fr/g-b-s-sarl-18d559a4), [Abidjan.net business announcements](https://business.abidjan.net), [Baxtel Côte d'Ivoire data centers](https://baxtel.com/data-center/ivory-coast-cote-d-ivoire), [Datacentermap Abidjan](https://www.datacentermap.com/ivory-coast/abidjan/) GBS's own hosting page, read 21 September 2026, offers space in its Kinshasa and Lubumbashi data centres; PeeringDB lists a GBS Datacenter in Gombe with two networks.

Domestic DRC private. [Data Center Map](https://www.datacentermap.com/c/united-sa/), [LinkedIn](https://cd.linkedin.com/company/united-sa), [Info-Clipper](https://www.info-clipper.com/fr/entreprise/congo/ste-united-sa.cdde341t1.html), [United RDC](https://unitedrdc.com/) United's About page names Hussein Ibrahim as General Administrator and Ali Ibrahim as Director of Operations and says three brothers founded the company in 2018; its shareholders are not published.

facilities.name: ARPCE Data Center Brazzaville (2021)
facilities.operator: ARPCE (Agence de Regulation des Postes et Communications Electroniques)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: First ARPCE DC built in Brazzaville in 2021. Confirmed existing prior to 2024 Pointe-Noire launch. Also referenced: Ministry of Finance and MTN Congo had DCs in Brazzaville as of 2021 per ARPCE website. No published capacity specs. WACS/2Africa cable connects via Pointe-Noire. CG-IX IXP referenced but details sparse.. [DCD](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/african-development-bank-to-build-data-center-in-the-republic-of-congo/) [Agence Ecofin](https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0808-130708-congo-le-datacenter-national-est-acheve-a-90-a-environ-quatre-mois-de-l-echeance) [Sika Finance](https://www.sikafinance.com/marches/congo-lachevement-du-data-center-national-bloque-par-un-defaut-de-financement-gouvernemental_57001) [Sinomach](https://www.sinomach.com.cn/en/MediaCenter/News/202409/t20240919_440007.html) Digital Business Africa (4 March 2024) confirms ARPCE's earlier Brazzaville data centre: Tier II, housed in ARPCE's technical building. ARPCE's data centre is in its technical building, commissioned by the Prime Minister on 10 August 2021 (Digital Business Africa). PeeringDB's 'Siège de l'ARPCE' facility record (updated September 2025, read 21 September 2026) hosts the CGIX-BZV exchange with nine networks, which is taken as evidence the site is operating; PeeringDB names ARPCE's head office, the 2024 source its technical building. Prime Minister Anatole Collinet Makosso inaugurated it on 10 August 2021 in a new ARPCE technical building, built over 15 months, that also houses three network operations and supervision centres and a terminal-approval laboratory; ARPCE said it would support the digitisation of public services, the electronic stamp and the Hub Digital (Digital Business Africa, 10 Aug 2021).

facilities.name: ARPCE Data Center Pointe-Noire (2Africa)
facilities.operator: ARPCE (Agence de Regulation des Postes et Communications Electroniques)

Built over two years by ARPCE. DCD places the new 2Africa CLS near the existing WACS CLS; it does not give the data centre's distance from either. MTN Congo also connected 2Africa at Pointe-Noire Feb 2026.. [DCD](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/african-development-bank-to-build-data-center-in-the-republic-of-congo/) [Agence Ecofin](https://www.agenceecofin.com/actualites-numerique/0808-130708-congo-le-datacenter-national-est-acheve-a-90-a-environ-quatre-mois-de-l-echeance) [Sika Finance](https://www.sikafinance.com/marches/congo-lachevement-du-data-center-national-bloque-par-un-defaut-de-financement-gouvernemental_57001) [Sinomach](https://www.sinomach.com.cn/en/MediaCenter/News/202409/t20240919_440007.html) The ministry (28 Feb 2024) calls it Tier 3+, with 18 racks in each of three containment zones, connected to both the WACS and 2Africa cables, and able to host public administration and private-sector data.

facilities.name: Congo National Data Center Brazzaville (AfDB/CAB)
facilities.operator: TBD (delegated manager to be appointed post-completion)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Three-storey building with basement (Sinomach: one underground and four above-ground floors) on the former UAPT site in Bacongo (2nd arrondissement), Brazzaville. EUR52.47m AfDB + EUR14.5m Govt = EUR66.55m total; DC component €13.8m ($14.6m) of the $72.8m CAB package; investment_usd is the DC component. 75% complete Mar 2025; 90% mid-2025 (Ecofin). Works halted at 95% in Oct 2025 over an unpaid government tranche, and the Chinese EPC contractor SUMEC threatened to withdraw (Sika Finance, 21 Oct 2025). Part of Central Africa Backbone (CAB) fibre project. Delegated operator to be named. GPS approximate (Bacongo district). [Energy Capital & Power](https://energycapitalpower.com/congos-national-data-center-in-brazzaville-reaches-75-completion/), [Data Center Dynamics](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/african-development-bank-to-build-data-center-in-the-republic-of-congo/), [AfDB Press](https://afdb.africa-newsroom.com/press/congo--le-nouveau-datacenter-finance-par-la-banque-africaine-de-developpement-va-consacrer-la-souverainete-numerique-du-pays-et-de-la-sousregion?lang=en), [ARPCE Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agence_de_R%C3%A9gulation_des_Postes_et_des_Communication_Electroniques_Republique_du_Congo) Minister Ibombo referred to the data centre's inauguration as done in January 2026 (ADIAC, 19 Jan 2026), but on a site visit on 11 February 2026 the AfDB president said equipment would be installed in the coming weeks and the inauguration would take place by May 2026, with all financing mobilised; that source calls it Tier III+ and gives the EUR66.55m CAB total as its cost. The ministry's programme page (September 2026) describes it in the present tense as hosting state data, without a commissioning date. Allo Brazza (22 May 2026) still reported it 95% complete, with opening due in May 2026 and the national cloud in June; a September 2026 search found no report of its inauguration, so it stays Under construction. At an inspection on 22 September 2026 the vice-prime minister put works at 82% and said the centre would be operational by the end of 2026 or early 2027, with energy tests within a month; a 12 MW solar farm at Kintele is to back it because the digital minister said grid power alone would deter clients. On 23 September 2026 the contractor SUMEC confirmed delivery by the end of 2026 (Sika Finance); backup power is three 3,000 kVA generators with two 40,000-litre tanks for 72 hours, and a grid and solar dual supply is being studied.

[Telecompaper data center article](https://www.telecompaper.com/news/comoros-completes-construction-of-public-administration-data-centre--1536505), [Comores Telecom site](https://comorestelecom.km/portail/pg/apropos/1), [World Bank RCIP report](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099082323102024792/pdf/P11821307cc1c003e0bf5709384bc41bafd.pdf), [APC Comores](https://access.apc.org/content/comores.html) In service by 6-7 May 2025, when it enabled ANADEN's takeover of the .km ccTLD, and inaugurated 19 May 2025 (Al-Watwan; ANADEN); Ecofin calls it a Tier 3-category facility with 44.4 terabits of hosting capacity, put back into service on a 2024 government decision. The AfDB-financed PADEC national data centre is a separate facility still to be built on the Universite des Comores campus (IsDB notice, March 2026); whether this is the 'existing secondary data centre' the same AfDB project funds is not stated. The government decided in 2024 to put the existing administration data centre back into service (Ecofin); HabarizaComores (May 2025) calls it the fruit of the World Bank's RCIP-4 project. The new national data centre PADEC is building on the Universite des Comores campus is a separate site (COM-002). ANADEN announced the inauguration for 19 May 2025, co-managed with Comores Câbles; Comores Câbles describes itself as a public enterprise (read September 2026). On 21 October 2026 the telecoms minister briefed the Council of Ministers on the takeover, operation and hosting of the state data centre and presented a national data-governance and data-centre strategy for 2027-2031; the report does not name the facility or an operator (Al-watwan, 22 October 2026).

facilities.name: Mohammadia National Data Center (DC1)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Algeria first national DC. Uptime Tier III Design cert obtained Feb 2026. Huawei-built in partnership with Ministry. ~80% operational. Dual power N+1 biometric access 24/7 monitoring. Working toward Tier III Facility Construction cert. Bekri Bouguerra Ave Mohammadia Algiers. [APS Algeria Press](https://www.aps.dz/fr/algerie/education-et-technologie/mlxxic0p-le-premier-data-center-national-obtient-une-certification-refletant-sa-maturite-technique-et-son-operationnalite), [DCD](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/algerian-govt-breaks-ground-on-ai-data-center-in-oran/), [Algeria Invest](https://algeriainvest.com/news/le-premier-data-center-national-obtient-une-certification-refletant-sa-maturite-technique-et-son-operationnalite), [Huawei](https://www.huawei.com/en/news/2025/2/algeria-400g) Inaugurated by President Tebboune on 5 July 2026 as the Mohammadia half of the Centre national algérien des services numériques (CNSN), run active-active with DZA-002 at a claimed 99.98% availability; it hosts the national cloud and the Dzair Digital Services portal (status as of 5 July 2026). The named tenants are users of the CNSN's national cloud, which spans both sites. Built by a Huawei-led consortium under a contract signed with the HCN in April 2024; inaugurated by President Tebboune on 5 July 2026 (DZWatch; DistantNews). The High Commission for Digitalisation signed the contract for the national digital services centre, with its two data centres at Algiers and Blida, with a Huawei consortium in April 2024 (El Watan, citing APS, July 2024). The Council of Ministers approved the project in November 2023 and the contract with Huawei Telecommunications Algeria was signed in April 2024 by direct negotiation; its value is not published (Maghreb Emergent, February 2026).

facilities.name: National Data Center 2 (DC2) Blida
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Under construction 50% complete Q1 2026. Government seeking Tier III Design cert from Uptime. Province of Blida ~50km SW of Algiers. Part of National Digital Transformation Strategy. No capacity specs published. [APS Algeria Press](https://www.aps.dz/fr/algerie/education-et-technologie/mlxxic0p-le-premier-data-center-national-obtient-une-certification-refletant-sa-maturite-technique-et-son-operationnalite), [DCD](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/algerian-govt-breaks-ground-on-ai-data-center-in-oran/), [Algeria Invest](https://algeriainvest.com/news/le-premier-data-center-national-obtient-une-certification-refletant-sa-maturite-technique-et-son-operationnalite), [Huawei](https://www.huawei.com/en/news/2025/2/algeria-400g) We Are Tech (8 July 2026) reports it running active-active with DZA-001 since the 5 July 2026 inauguration, but El Watan's report of that inauguration says the Blida centre is still to be built. Uptime Tier III Design certified September 2026; the HCN is still seeking Tier III Constructed Facility. The HCN's March 2025 communiqué has Algerian and Chinese staff building the first Blida unit; Huawei is named as builder of the two-site centre as a whole. Status as of July 2026: the national centre inaugurated on 5 July 2026 runs Mohammadia and Blida as an active-active pair (We Are Tech; DistantNews). Uptime's register lists the design certificate as HCN Bouarfa 09019, awarded 18 May 2026 and expiring 2028. The whole centre was contracted to a Huawei-led consortium (DZWatch, April 2024). Reports of the 5 July 2026 inauguration disagree: El Watan says the Blida site is still to be built, We Are Tech and DistantNews describe Algiers and Blida running active-active; Uptime's design-only award (May 2026) fits a site not yet built, so the status stays Under construction. Status as of July 2026: the Prime Minister's services said on 17 December 2025 that the second national data centre, still being finished, had been put into service on 26 September 2025 (Algerie 62), and the HCN's central director Mohamed Louail said in July 2026 that the national digital services centre runs its Mohammadia and Blida sites at the same time, active-active (El Massar, 14 July 2026). These official statements outweigh El Watan's report that Blida was still to be built; Uptime's design-only certificate does not show the site is unbuilt. In October 2025 the minister put construction of the Blida centre at 75% complete (Algerie 54).

Uptime Institute's register (checked September 2026) lists four further Ethio Telecom sites with Tier III design certification: Nefas Silk, Old Airport and Tikur Anbessa in Addis Ababa, and Debre Birhan DC01; each now has its own row. Nearly 90 enterprise customers were co-located here by May 2022, after the five leases signed that month (Further Africa, 24 May 2022). Ethio Telecom's CEO said in October 2022, launching its Huawei-built TeleCloud, that modular data centres were built or under construction at four Addis Ababa sites, 5.2 MW of IT load and 640 racks in all, with more planned in regional towns (The Reporter).

Floor space is the site ('more than 3,000 m2'); phase 1 has a 65 m2 colocation room. 1 MW is installed electrical capacity, not an IT-only figure, with phased increases planned; about 22% of energy from on-site solar. ITWeb says it connects to the ACE and SAT-3 cables and to national operators by peering; a room is set aside for AI uses. [GDCL website](https://www.gdcl.gov.gh), [NITA DCD article](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/ghana-government-opens-data-center-to-private-business/), [GDCL YouTube CEO](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qXklJgwYXnc), [NITA site](https://nita.gov.gh/projects/datacentre/) The World Bank's eTransform project (closed June 2024) funded a government cloud data centre and a 1,289TB cloud storage system, 703TB in Accra and 586TB in Kumasi. The government says the National Data Centre is being modernised for AI services (July 2026) and its upgrade is part of a US$200M digitalisation project (September 2026); scope and cost of the upgrade are not given. GhanaWeb (September 2024) says the data centre is managed by NITA's private sector partner, Smart Infraco. The government tendered a World Bank-funded 'National Data Center Refresh and Upgrade' in June 2026. Launched January 2016 with a secondary centre at KNUST, Kumasi, both run by NITA with Huawei and Alcatel Lucent (Graphic Online). The June 2026 World Bank-financed tender for a refresh says both centres have run for 10 years and are about 90% full, with Huawei network equipment at end of support; the Accra building has engineering on the ground floor and two data-hall floors, the first commissioned and the second reserved, each with six small halls; the upgrade fits out white space F5 for 68 racks and adds AI infrastructure. At a Public Accounts Committee hearing in August 2025, auditors reported that Smart Infraco, which took over Lebara Ghana's contract to commercialise spare capacity in the e-government infrastructure including the national data centre, had paid none of the $6m in advances due to the state for 2020-2024; NITA said the company denied owing the sums and the ministry had referred the matter to the Attorney-General (Ghanaian Chronicle, 20 August 2025).

facilities.name: Guinea National Tier III Data Centre
facilities.operator: Not yet appointed (Ministry of Communication, Digital Economy and Innovation responsible)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Inaugurated 4 Sep 2025. Tier 3 certified by Uptime Institute. Technical details not publicly disclosed. Mentioned at Transform Africa Summit Nov 2025 as symbol of digital sovereignty. GPS is approximate Conakry government district. Supports .GN domain reinstatement.. [Ecofin Agency inauguration](https://www.ecofinagency.com/news-digital/0409-48427-guinea-opens-tier-3-national-data-center-to-strengthen-digital-transition), [Africa24 TV](https://africa24tv.com/guinee-inauguration-du-premier-data-center-national), [Tech Africa News](https://techafricanews.com/2025/09/05/guinea-launches-national-domain-gn-and-unveils-first-tier-iii-data-center/), [Smart Africa](https://smartafrica.org/transform-africa-summit-2025-conakry-becomes-the-epicenter-of-digital-cooperation-in-africa/) Sited at Koloma, Conakry. Inaugurated 4 September 2025 but not in service by September 2026: on a site visit on 9 September 2026 the Prime Minister put execution at about 90% and investment at close to US$10 million (government-funded, total project), cited an outstanding payment, and asked for it to be brought into service within weeks, possibly under an interim manager; the ministry says it will host government and private data. Previously held by the Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and Digital Economy. In July 2026 the ministry discussed operationalisation with Groupe COREX and a national data centre and sovereign cloud with Huawei; neither is agreed. Guinéenews (14 September 2026): the Koloma data centre is about 90% complete at about US$10M and not yet operational. Le Djely (4 September 2025): over 600 m² with two 90 m² IT rooms. Ecofin, Le Djely and others report Uptime Tier III certification without saying whether it covers the design documents or the constructed facility. Corex Senegal's director general said at the opening that it is equipped with 100 TB of storage, to be extended to 5,000 TB across two rooms (Emedia, September 2025). Le360 Afrique (15 March 2026): Groupe Corex's director general says the design and construction phase closed with the inauguration and the site has not yet been handed to the state, with Corex in talks to run and maintain it; the site has two grid feeds from opposite ends of the city backed by generators, both down on the day of the visit.

[Gambia Gov Cloud Strategy](https://mocde.gov.gm/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Gambia-G-Cloud-Strategy-document_Final-Draft.pdf), [Gamtel Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gambia_Telecommunications_Company), [AidData China Exim GNBN](https://china.aiddata.org/projects/56878), [Gamtel site](https://gamtel.gm), [WBBA Gamtel Case](https://worldbroadbandassociation.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/WBBA-GAMTEL_Final.pdf) SIXP's own administrator (AfPIF 2015) dates its establishment to July 2014, not 2013, and reports no carrier-neutral data centres in the country. The Gambia National Broadband Network project (China Eximbank loan, Huawei EPC, completed June 2019) included a US$3.4M data centre that Gamtel was mandated to manage from 2019 (Foroyaa, July 2020); the G-Cloud strategy calls it a Tier-2 national data centre managed by Gamtel and underused. No source places it at the Kairaba exchange; whether it is this facility is unconfirmed. The World Bank's digital economy diagnostic (2021) calls the Exim-financed government centre managed by Gamtel Tier-3, says its use is limited because backup systems were not yet in place, and that it was not fully operational; it does not give its site.

facilities.name: Konza National Data Centre (KoTDA)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Built by Huawei (EPC contractor) under a China Eximbank concessional loan of RMB 1.225bn (~US$200M, Ksh17bn, signed April 2019) for the data centre and smart city project; containerized Phase 1 complete 2020; Tier III design Phase 2 complete 2021; supports 70+ city services; 120+ customers (75% govt); Huawei Cloud Stack. KSh3.1B budget 2025/26. Operational per the Treasury's Konza Cloud Expansion RFP addendum (April 2026): storage 100% used, about 70% of racks in use, 145 of 451 government institutions hosted; nine ISPs and a Radware PoP connected; an on-site IXP is planned. Landlocked (4 hrs from coast); [KenGen Announcement](https://www.kengen.co.ke/index.php/information-center/news-and-events/kengen-teams-up-with-microsoft-and-g42-for-$1b-cutting-edge-green-data-center-in-olkaria.html), [Kenyan Wallstreet](https://kenyanwallstreet.com/kengen-first-state-firm-comply-new-goe-law), [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenya_Electricity_Generating_Company), [MarketScreener](https://www.marketscreener.com/quote/stock/KENYA-ELECTRICITY-GENERAT-9295413/company-shareholders/) Business Daily (August 2026) calls it fully state-owned, with KSh175 million allocated for expansion in FY2026/27. UNDP is supporting a national AI computing platform with NVIDIA GPUs at KoTDA (July 2026), and KoTDA signed an agreement with AWS on 18 August 2026 for an AWS Outpost at Konza; neither source says which facility will house them. UNDP Kenya and the Technopolis Development Authority signed a Letter of Agreement to operationalise sovereign AI infrastructure at the facility for the AI Accelerator programme (reported 11 September 2026). A KoTDA feasibility study (2026) describes the facility as a multi-zone Tier III cloud near its resource limits, on an OpenStack-based KVM platform, and proposes a Cloud Expansion Project as a DBFOT PPP with a 36-month implementation; Treasury listed it among 13 priority PPP projects presented in Seoul in September 2026. KoTDA's ToR (March 2026): built from 2019, completed 2021. The KoTDA-AWS agreement (August 2026) provides for an AWS Outpost at Konza with no timeline or site named; not counted as a hyperscaler relationship until deployed. On 23 October 2026 the PPP Directorate announced a project-preparation funding agreement with KoTDA, from the Treasury's PPP Project Facilitation Fund, to hire a transaction adviser and carry out feasibility work for the Konza National Data Centre Cloud Expansion and Smart City Facilities Project, in the PPP pipeline since December 2025; no private partner has been chosen and no construction has started (People Daily; Tech Africa News, 23 October 2026).

[EcoCloud site](https://ecocloud.co.ke/about/), [MSFT-G42 Kenya](https://news.microsoft.com/source/2024/05/22/microsoft-and-g42-announce-1-billion-comprehensive-digital-ecosystem-initiative-for-kenya/), [G42 Wiki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G42_(company)), [PRNewswire MoU](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/president-of-kenya-unveils-green-powered-mega-data-center-in-collaboration-with-the-uae-setting-stage-for-kenya-as-a-global-digital-hub-302082899.html) Microsoft-G42 Kenya project put on hold in May 2026: the government balked at the fiscal and energy guarantees and President Ruto said powering it would take too much of the grid (Atlantic Council, 31 Jul 2026; LinkedIn analysis, 17 Aug 2026). TechCabal (11 June 2026) reports the Microsoft/G42 Olkaria project on hold, with talks stalled over power and financing; Rest of World (20 August 2026) says Kenya suspended it over grid constraints. Also covers the former KEN-029 (Microsoft Azure East Africa Cloud Region): G42's plan for this campus, built with EcoCloud as local partner, was 100MW initially and up to 1GW, to run Azure. On hold since May 2026: the President said the grid could not supply it and the Treasury had not approved the government's share; Bloomberg reports the partners may scale it back, with talks on a smaller 60MW EcoCloud facility; the site was unbuilt in 2026. The USD 600 million is the value the energy minister gave the EcoCloud centre at its 2023 groundbreaking (KNA). KenGen told Al Jazeera in August 2026 that the Microsoft-G42 centre remains at the design stage.

facilities.name: Nouakchott Data Hub
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Inaugurated May 8 2025 by President Ghazaouani. Tier III certified by Uptime Institute. EIB €15M loan via WARCIP. Operator IMT/GIE is JV of state (Mauripost) and three telecoms. First national data centre. SDIN is holding entity. Ellalink second submarine cable announced July 2025.. [FT_EPIC_2021 PDF](https://www.finances.gov.mr/sites/default/files/2022-12/FT_EPIC_2021_DTF_-_Nov2822.pdf), [Rapport EP 2020 PDF](https://www.finances.gov.mr/sites/default/files/2022-12/Rapport_de_PR_2020-1.pdf), [MTNIMA](https://mtnima.gov.mr/fr/les-entites-sous-tutelle/), [Uptime Institute](https://uptimeinstitute.com/component/tierachievement/client/socit-pour-le-dveloppement-des-infrastructures-numriques-sdin/800) Operator: Al Wiam (11 August 2026) reports AN-ETAT, the state digital agency, runs and operates the centre; the EIB and EEAS (2025) had said IMT/GIE would operate it once operational. AMI (8 May 2025) gives 1,372 m2, not saying whether building or white space, and 100 racks. The national government cloud was launched at the centre on 29 June 2026 (Ecofin); on 2 July 2026 the minister told the National Assembly all public-administration servers had been moved there, on hyperconverged infrastructure. In April 2024 SOMELEC's distribution company tendered the supply and commissioning of the national data centre's connection to two 15 kV delivery substations (4 x 800 kVA) from its Nord substation (DCCO 09/CAE/2024). G42, through G42 Cloud and Presight, signed an MoU with the digital ministry on 31 May 2023 to work on the national data centre and a national sovereign cloud; no G42 role at this facility has been reported since (Presight, 7 June 2023). Mauritania's personal data protection authority met AN-ETAT and the operating telecoms company on 10 June 2026 to discuss localising AN-ETAT's data and accrediting the Nouakchott data centre under data protection law 2017-020 (Ettayar). On 4 June 2026 AN-ETAT signed a three-year renewable agreement with the Mauritanian International Telecommunications company (IMT) to host its data at the Nouakchott data centre, with IMT providing secure high-bandwidth connectivity and continuous power (Eljedid News, citing the digital ministry); this casts IMT as the hosting provider and AN-ETAT as a tenant, against Al Wiam's August 2026 account of AN-ETAT running the centre.

facilities.note: Tier IV Uptime certified design and constructed; 1500sqm white space; 3MW IT load; ISO 27001:2013; Govt-majority ownership (Govt 40% + NPF + SBM ~59%). Sovereign cloud expansion and GPU cluster investment announced 2025. SAFE; LION; MARS; 2Africa submarine cable access via Mauritius Telecom.. [Ministry of Social Security NPF page](https://socialsecurity.govmu.org/socialsecurity/?page_id=1216), [NPF Portfolio page](https://socialsecurity.govmu.org/socialsecurity/?page_id=1217), [SWFI Profile](https://www.swfinstitute.org/profile/598cdaa60124e9fd2d05b8e5), [OECD IOPS Profile](https://www.oecd.org/content/dam/iops/en/country-profiles/MauritiusPensionSystemProfile.pdf) The ICT minister (L'Express, 31 December 2025) says Rose-Belle hosts the government's e-Health system, the new government portal, Mobile ID, the penalty-points software and government AI equipment, and serves as backup to the Government Online Centre at Ebene; MITCI's sovereign-cloud RFI (September 2025) calls it the GOC's Tier IV certified secondary site, ISO 27001 compliant. GPU capability rests on MT's CEO, who said on 16 July 2026 that NVIDIA H200s are installed in MT's data centre (not named) and B300s are due by year end; in February 2026 he had said B300s carried a one-year lead time. Investment: more than Rs 1 billion (Le Mauricien, 28 March 2024), about USD 21.7M at March 2024 rates, for the facility as built. ISO 27001:2022 per the MSB register (31 December 2025), expiring 24 September 2028. Mauritius Telecom's CEO said in July 2026 that NVIDIA H200 GPUs are in 'our data centre', without naming the site. Mauritius Telecom launched its my.t cloud services, including Elastic Cloud Servers, at the Rose Belle data centre on 27 March 2024; the CEO put the data centre's cost at over Rs 1 billion (Le Mauricien; Defi Media). The MSB register (31 December 2025) lists Mauritius Telecom's ISO 27001:2022 certificate (ISM 008), covering Rose Belle (Business Parks of Mauritius, Gros Billot, New Grove) and Rose Hill, issued 25 September 2025 and expiring 24 September 2028.

[ESCOM ISP27](https://www.escom.mw/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Integrated-Strategic-Plan-ISP27_Final30_08_2023.pdf), [PPPC](https://digmap.pppc.mw/government-data-centre-project-completion-at-77/), [Datacentermap](https://www.datacentermap.com/malawi/blantyre/malawi-national-data-center/), [People.cn](https://en.people.cn/n3/2022/0723/c90000-10126559.html) Financing: Malawi's Parliament authorised a US$56.9M China Construction Bank loan for the Last Mile Connectivity for Rural Area and National Data Centre Project on 25 January 2019, after repealing an ICBC loan for the same project (AidData); the loan also covers rural towers, so it is not the facility's cost alone. Operated by the Ministry of Information and Digitalisation, ESCOM and Huawei (MBC, February 2024; Times, April 2025). ESCOM's 2025 ITU presentation gives 2 modules of 21 racks at 6 kW a rack and says the centre is open to government and private clients. Malawi's Act 22 of 2018 authorises an ICBC loan for the National Data Centre Project; whether and how much was disbursed is not stated. The OFC/ESCOM Tier 3 data centre row (MWI-004) described this facility and is folded into it. ESCOM said in February 2024 that the centre hosted about 78 virtual machines, one client each, up from ten clients four months after the July 2022 launch, drawn from ministries, agencies and the private sector (MBC, 10 February 2024).

facilities.name: Malawi Government Data Centre Lilongwe
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Constructed under World Bank Digital Malawi Foundations Project. Primary govt DC; Blantyre (MWI-001) is backup. HCI (Hyper-Converged Infrastructure). Opened ~2025. Bomalathu data exchange platform deployed. Expansion ongoing under Digital Malawi Acceleration Project (USD 150M World Bank from Nov 2024).. [ESCOM ISP27](https://www.escom.mw/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/Integrated-Strategic-Plan-ISP27_Final30_08_2023.pdf), [PPPC](https://digmap.pppc.mw/government-data-centre-project-completion-at-77/), [Datacentermap](https://www.datacentermap.com/malawi/blantyre/malawi-national-data-center/), [People.cn](https://en.people.cn/n3/2022/0723/c90000-10126559.html) Works were unfinished when the Digital Foundations Project closed on 31 October 2024 and passed to DMAP (ESMP, August 2025), which lists 13 empty server racks for colocation. The June 2026 expansion RFB describes a Tier-III production site with a 105 kW design IT load, 20 kW in use; IT power is that design load. In June 2026 the ICT minister discussed a US$180M ICT investment plan with Huawei in China; talks only. September 2026 reports still list the centre's operationalisation among DMAP's aims. Commissioning was due May 2025 (Times, April 2025) and operation June 2025 (Malawi Guardian, May 2025); running at partial load per the June 2026 RFB, and ITWeb (3 September 2026) still lists its operationalisation under DMAP. Expansion: the DMAP ESMP plans added server equipment, a DR fibre link to Blantyre and a service power line. The Department of e-Government's managed-services terms of reference (January 2025) place the facility in Area 4, Lilongwe, next to the department's offices, running on Nutanix NX-3460-G7 hyperconverged nodes (277.2 GHz, 2.63 TB memory) with 13 empty racks for colocation; it and the Blantyre DR site are described as Tier III facilities (not a certification). A US$20m expansion is the largest planned procurement under the World Bank's Digital Malawi Acceleration Project; the centre hosted six ministry databases as of November 2025, and prospective bidders raised vendor lock-in concerns in October 2025. A World Bank implementation mission (September 2026) calls the US$10m expansion of the national data centre the project's largest contract, to host more government systems beyond the eleven already there; the e-Government department withdrew the bidding document for revision in late August 2026, due back to the Bank by 11 September. A fibre link to the Blantyre backup site (MWI-001) has been commissioned and a backup power line procured (World Bank DMAP aide-memoire, September 2026). The service power line is an 11 kV underground cable of about 1.5 km from the Kamuzu Central Hospital substation, with a new transformer, funded under the Digital Malawi Acceleration Project (PPPC environmental and social management plan, June 2025).

facilities.name: Sudatel Data Centre Khartoum
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Claimed largest DC in North and East Africa at build; 14000sqm; 4 data rooms; ~4000 server capacity; Tier III+ design. CONFLICT IMPACT: April 2023 civil war damaged Khartoum infrastructure; facility status uncertain. EASSy; FALCON; TEAMS cables at Port Sudan. SIXP IXP listed Defunct (PCH). [Wikipedia Sudatel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudatel), [Mubasher Profile](https://english.mubasher.info/markets/adx/stocks/SUDATEL/profile), [Actum Sudan State DC](https://actumsudan.substack.com/p/sudan-pushes-digital-transformation), [Sudatel Website](https://www.sudatel.sd) Sudatel's own page calls SDC a Tier IV design with 99.995% availability (sudani.sd, captured 2024). In January 2026 Sudani's deputy director general for operations said the company had lost the Tier-4 data centre that hosted the state government and institutions, along with the Abu Haraz satellite station, and resumed service by restoring a separate core data centre (CGTN, 7 January 2026). Sudani's operations CEO told CGTN (January 2026) the Khartoum Tier-4 data centre was lost; the Port Sudan Tier III data centre has its own row. Leading Edge Guides (2016, company figures): a US$45m build; the 14,000 m2 is the whole site, with four data rooms totalling 1,424 m2 for up to 700 racks. It dates the inauguration to 2015; Africa Outlook dates the launch to December 2014. SMEX (May 2023) reports that the Sudanese Armed Forces announced on 23 April 2023 that the RSF had occupied the Sudatel Centre, the old exchange building housing Sudatel's data centres, cutting Sudani's services until the next day.

facilities.name: Diamniadio National Datacenter
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: 500 sqm hosting capacity phase 1; CFA 46bn ($18.2M) Chinese Eximbank loan; Huawei equipment/tech support; inaugurated 22 Jun 2021 by President Macky Sall; all govt data mandated to migrate here; self-declared tier standard (Smart Senegal/Tier III references in govt docs); Huawei stack creates high foreign dependency.. [Data Center Map](https://www.datacentermap.com/c/senegal-numerique-sa-adie/), [DCD](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/senegal-to-migrate-all-government-data-and-applications-to-new-government-data-center/), [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/article/technology/senegal-aims-for-digital-sovereignty-with-new-china-backed-data-centre-idUSL5N2O44D3/), [US State Dept](https://www.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/senegal) Hosts the TAQUEY supercomputer with GPUs for AI workloads, which supported SEN-GENOME (Global Center on AI Governance brief, August 2026); GPU models not named. SENUM (2025) gives the Diamniadio centre 1,000 TB of storage at 31% utilisation and prints a cost of 83bn FCFA beside it without saying what the figure covers. The building cost CFA 10bn, per ADIE's network director (Dakaractu, June 2021) and CIO Mag (23 June 2021), which matches DCD's $18.2M; DCD's and RFI's CFA 46bn is a larger figure, not this facility's cost. Alibaba Cloud's Apsara Stack national cloud (received 24 March 2026) was installed in SENUM's data centres without the site being named. President Sall announced a Smart Sénégal phase 2 at the 2021 inauguration; no source says what it builds here. CIO Mag (23 June 2021) values the facility at FCFA 10bn, which is the US$18.2M recorded as the investment (at mid-2021 rates); it describes a Tier 3 build on over 1 ha with 1,000 TB of storage and 99.982% availability, built with Huawei after three years of works. The FCFA 46bn above is not the build cost. Under a framework agreement signed in late January 2024, SENUM is to host the health ministry's applications in the national data centre, including the shared single patient record and emergency management, and to move the DHIS2 health-information platform there from Linode (Sud Quotidien, February 2024). ADIE's director general put it at nearly 1,000 m2 of technical rooms and 1.4 MW at the June 2021 inauguration (Jonction/CIPESA, citing RFI). APS (27 May 2025) places the Taouey supercomputer at the Cite du Savoir in Diamniadio under CINERI, and says CINERI wants a data centre of its own like the one SENUM holds at Diamniadio, so the Taouey hosting claim above is doubtful; Taouey has its own row. A DPI Africa investigation (May 2025), citing PressAfrik, found that apart from the health ministry, about 80% migrated, no public or private institution had moved its data to Diamniadio despite the 2021 instruction, and that national ID card data remained hosted abroad. At the June 2021 opening the technical zone held two 250 m2 halls with four pods of 18 racks, 1,000 TB of initial storage, three telecom rooms and three generators (Socialnetlink); the rack count is that figure. In October 2026 the centre's manager, Ousmane Bop, said 10-20% of Senegal's public data was still hosted abroad, held there by hosting contracts of up to ten years; the state is weighing buying them out or waiting for them to expire (Senego, citing KOOM Business TV).

facilities.name: RSTP National Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: RSTP Innovation Park Phocweni Matsapha M202. Self-declared Tier III 99.982% uptime. 24/7 surveillance biometric access. Hot DR site planned ~50km away. Primary govt DC for Eswatini. Year operational unknown.. [RSTP Data Centre](https://rstp.org.sz/national-data-centre/), [RSTP Home](https://rstp.org.sz), [Gov SOE Framework](https://www.gov.sz/images/FinanceDocuments/SOE-Restructuring-Framework-in-Eswatini.pdf), [Datacentermap RSTP](https://www.datacentermap.com/eswatini/mbabane/rstp-national-data-center/) RSTP's 2023 brochure says a hot DR site is to be built about 50 km from the primary site, financed by a US$10.4M India Exim line of credit (2021); whether it is built is not stated. February 2026: the ICT minister discussed dedicated renewable power for the NDC with UAE-based Global South Utilities (talks only). A May 2026 government assessment found ministries depend almost entirely on RSTP for hosting, a 'structural concentration risk'. September 2026: the finance minister told Parliament the disaster recovery site in Lubombo had not proceeded, the US$10.4M India Exim loan was undrawn and government had applied to cancel it; he said a functional primary data centre was needed first and that the RSTP facility did not constitute a fully operational data centre (Times of Eswatini, 22 September; Independent News, 23 September). On 23 September 2026 the ICT ministry acknowledged outages across government online services, including e-Visa, deeds registration and the financial management system; a reported breach of RSTP systems with a EUR 1M ransom demand was unconfirmed. An incident at the National Data Centre, first acknowledged as a web-services outage on 18 September 2026, disrupted at least 12 government digital services including Government in Your Hand, e-Visa, IFMIS and online company registration; RSTP confirmed the incident on 24 September 2026 but not social-media claims of a hack or ransom demand. September 2026 incident disrupted at least 12 government services; police engaged INTERPOL and will investigate after the consultant's report, with preliminary findings of corrupted files and no data stolen (2026-09-28). The finance ministry said in October 2026 that the India Exim Bank loan for the disaster recovery site has not been cancelled: 1% was disbursed for project development, and the lender has agreed to stop the commitment fees on the undrawn balance. The 2020 budget speech (14 February 2020) described the National Data Centre as operational and said funding had been secured for a data recovery centre. In April 2025 the ICT minister said some banks and telecoms had chosen not to use the park's data centre and that the long-term aim was a Tier III centre at RSTP (Eswatini Observer, 13 April 2025), which sits uneasily with the self-declared Tier III above. A consultant who visited in late 2019 describes the centre as recently launched, at Tier III level, offering colocation and basic cloud (TechPlus+, 2025). The ICT minister said in October 2024 that RSTP plans two further Tier 4 centres; no site or date was given (Inside Biz).

facilities.note: Under construction as of early 2026. Part of EUR175.1m ($204.7m) PMICE Phase I (Eximbank-financed). Includes 1,200km fibre deployment. Inauguration ceremony held Sarh Dec 2025. Location assumed N'Djamena; no confirmed address. Landlocked ( No IXP. Huawei equipment likely (Airtel replacing Ericsson core with Huawei). investment_usd reflects full PMICE Phase I not DC component alone.. [Data Center Dynamics](https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/chad-invests-175m-in-national-data-center-and-networks/), [World Bank PDF](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099102502282341480/pdf/P180000048eed6040a13200ddaf8abe650.pdf), [SOTEL Presentation](https://www.scribd.com/document/957684591/PRESENTATION-OF-THE-SOTEL-GROUP-CHAD-1), [Trade.gov](https://www.trade.gov/country-commercial-guides/chad-telecommunications) The main centre is at Klemat, N'Djamena, with a secondary centre at Farcha (ATPE, June 2023). Built by Huawei Technologies with GOLF/Gulf Consultancy as supervising engineer under the China EXIM-financed PMICE (Agence Ecofin, January 2025; Digital Business Africa, May 2026); the building is 500 m2 spread over four levels (building, not white space) with a 750 kVA generator. ADETIC, ANSICE and TECHSO-GROUP signed a security audit and certification agreement on 5 February 2026; on 19 May 2026 the building and equipment were complete but certification was outstanding, and on 1 July 2026 Cybastion was to help audit it before operation. The minister announced two data centres commissioned at N'Djamena on 7 August 2026. The World Bank (September 2024) said the Exim-funded data centre does not comply with international standards. SOTEL was named as operator before 2026 sources. A September 2026 search found no report after the minister's 7 August statement, no inauguration and no certification result; status rests on that statement. Bandeinfo (31 May 2023) places the main data centre at Klemat, N'Djamena, where the minister was shown a model of the building; the secondary site is at Farcha (TCD-002).

facilities.name: Lomé Data Centre (LDC)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Togo's first carrier-neutral facility, inaugurated Jun 2021 by President Gnassingbé. Owned by SIN (state), operated by Africa Data Centres (ADC, a Cassava Technologies business). $23.7M World Bank WARCIP funding. Tier III+ per website; PUE 1.4. Direct access to ACE, WACS, 2Africa, Equiano cables. Togo Law 2019-014 data protection applies.. [Liquid Zambia acquisition](https://liquid.tech/about-us/news/liquid_intelligent_technologies_completes_acquisition_of_cec_liquid_intelligent_technologies_in_zambia_to_further_strengthen_its_operations_in_southern_africa/), [Cassava funding](https://www.cassavatechnologies.com/secures-usd-310-million-in-funding-and-completes-business-reorganisation/), [Liquid board](https://liquid.tech/investor-centre/board-of-directors/), [Data centre pledge](https://www.connectingafrica.com/data-centers/liquid-intelligent-technologies-to-build-data-center-in-zambia) SIN's release (26 May 2026) and Connecting Africa (2 June 2026) name SIN, wholly owned by the state, as the LDC's operator and call it Tier III certified; Africa Data Centres, the operator the row previously named, is not mentioned. SIN and ST DIGITAL signed an MoU on 26 May 2026 to sell private cloud services on LDC infrastructure. Data protection claims refer to Togo Law 2019-014. ADC's management contract ran five years from 2021 (RFI, July 2021); the government authorised handing LDC to a private manager in December 2022 and was still seeking one in July 2023 (DCmag). PeeringDB (September 2025) lists SIN as the facility's organisation. Togo First (June 2021): five server hosting rooms of 133 m2 each (665 m2 in all, against the row's 500 m2), four for private operators, each with 36 bays (180 racks); power is a redundant 1 MW primary supply plus two 1,000 kVA generators, total facility power rather than IT load. RFI (July 2021) and DCmag (July 2023) put the World Bank-financed cost at $30M, against DCD's $23.7M. UNDP (3 November 2026): a GPU server donated by UNDP, in service at the centre since July 2026 and run by Togo AI Lab, gives Togo its first national AI compute; between 26 August and 27 October 2026 it handled about 50,200 model requests with no data passed to an outside provider. The GPU model is not stated.

facilities.name: INFRATEL Primary Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: National DC origin; evolved from ZICTA/Smart Zambia Zambia-China bilateral project. Primary facility UN Rd & Independence Ave Stand 4909 Lusaka; 1.25MW; biometric access; 100% carrier neutral. Floor space is Huawei's figure for the whole main centre at ZICTA; racks are its count of server cabinets. DPA 2021 applies. submarine_cable_access=4 (landlocked).. [Infratel Profile](https://infratel.co.zm/company-profile/), [IDC About](https://www.idc.co.zm/about-us/), [Smart Zambia](https://www.szi.gov.zm), [D4D Hub](https://cms.d4dhub.eu/assets/Initiatives/Data-Governance-in-Africa/Digital-Investment-Facility/2507_Country-Market-Briefs/Data-Center-Market-Brief-Zambia.pdf), [Huawei Case](https://e.huawei.com/ma/ict-insights/global/ict-new-horizons-podcasts/Stories/zambia) Phase 1 of Smart Zambia (this and the two backup centres, plus an ICT training centre) was financed by a US$65.47M China Eximbank concessional loan signed March 2015, paying for a Huawei contract of January 2015; implementation began January 2016. The Smart Zambia Phase I contract between the government and Huawei (2012) totals US$65,551,150 for the national data centre, a disaster-recovery data centre and ICT talent training, paid through the Export-Import Bank of China; the per-site split is not legible in the published copy, so it is not recorded as this facility's investment. The China Exim concessional loan was signed in March 2015; Phase II was cancelled in 2022 (Georgetown Africa-China Initiative, November 2025). Lusaka Times (5 January 2015) reported that the Huawei contract was single-sourced: no public tender was issued and the Zambia Public Procurement Authority issued its clearance only after signature.

GPU models not named. Sited at the CSIR campus, 15 Lower Hope Street, Rosebank, Cape Town (CHPC). facilities.name: Africa Data Centres Egypt
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Announced 8 September 2026 by Egypt's MCIT with Vodafone Business, Cassava Technologies and Elsewedy Electric as a joint venture for a sovereign AI data centre programme (iAfrikan, 11 September 2026). Investment is the $1 billion headline for the eventual build; about $200 million of foreign direct investment is committed to the first phase. IT power is the 20MW first phase; the long-run target is 200MW. Shareholdings not stated. The announcements of 8 September 2026 describe two partnerships: this joint venture of Vodafone Business, Elsewedy Electric and Cassava Technologies, and a separate Vodafone Business-Cassava 'AI factory' offering NVIDIA GPU-as-a-Service, launched in September 2026 with no site stated. The $1bn and 200 MW belong to this joint venture, not to the AI facility. Billionaires.Africa (10 September 2026) reports the Vodafone-Cassava sovereign AI data centre will sit inside the wider ADC Egypt project, so it has no row of its own; the site is still not stated. The sovereign AI data centre (GPU-as-a-Service with Cassava) is a secondary role inside the wider project. As of 10 September 2026 neither the partners nor MCIT had said where the campus will be or how the stakes are split (HCN Times). Vodacom's group technology chief said in October 2026 the facility will carry the group's own GPUs in two spaces, one for internal and one for external use, with phase one expected to draw about US$200m (Business Day).

facilities.name: Cybastion Douala AI Data Centre

facilities.name: ZAP Lobito Data Center (3 Casas)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: ZAP installed a data centre at the 3 Casas condominium in Lobito as the technical and data-management platform for its internet and television services along the Benguela coast; inaugurated by the telecoms minister on 2 September 2026 (Angop). No capacity or investment stated. ZAP's 70% holder, Zap Media (99.9% Finstar, Isabel dos Santos), was seized by a Luanda court in December 2019, and the government put ZAP Media and Finstar under a management commission in January 2022 (Lusa); no later change of ownership was found.

facilities.name: INP-HB Data Centre (Yamoussoukro)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Ivoirematin (17 September 2026) reports a data centre installed at the Institut national polytechnique Felix Houphouet-Boigny (INP-HB) in Yamoussoukro to store, process and secure the public administration's data for e-government. It gives no commissioning date, capacity, cost, owner or operator. Correction: AIP (17 September 2026) reports a technical visit to the site of the future PARAE data centre at the INP-HB Technopole, a 5,000 m² plot extended to 1 ha, with the AfDB, BNETD (owner's assistant) and the project unit; the data centre is planned, not installed.
