No operator is named. The AfDB environmental and social study (2022) names ANSUT as the promoter, which asked the prefect for the plot in July 2020, and describes a national public data centre with a CSIRT/SOC/PKI platform; the whole PARAE project is CFA 7.22 billion, the data centre's share not stated. Sika Finance (22 September 2026): planned to a Tier III design with duplicated power and cooling, 75% renewable energy at opening and 100% by 2035, for the state's internal use only, distinct from Cybastion's national data centre at Grand-Bassam (CIV-007); PARAE has a FCFA 60bn budget (January 2025 to 2028), of which EUR 54.54m for green digital infrastructure, the data centre's own share not stated. AIP (22 September 2026): the PARAE steering committee on 18 September 2026 noted delays and measures to start the works, and called for reviews to speed equipment procurement; works had not begun. The AfDB's supervision report on its January 2026 mission (published 30 July 2026) budgets the data centre at EUR 30m, the project's central investment: works procurement had not been launched, technical studies were being prepared with BNETD and the Bluebird consultancy, the land title for the roughly 5,000 m² INP-HB site was not yet secured, and the construction contract was targeted for September 2026.

facilities.name: Oran AI High-Performance Computing Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Algeria's first high-performance computing centre dedicated to AI; the Minister of Post and Telecommunications laid its foundation stone on 16 March 2025, for use by researchers, start-ups and academic institutions, to be equipped with latest-generation GPUs (We Are Tech, 17 March 2025). Two July 2026 reports (Le Jeune Indépendant, We Are Tech) say an AI data centre in Oran was put into service in March 2025, the month of the groundbreaking, so whether it is in service is unresolved. GPU models not named. Algérie Télécom's project, foundation stone laid 16 March 2025 in Akid Lotfi, east Oran, near the Méridien hotel (TSA, El Watan); AlgeriaTech (April 2026) says it is still under construction, so the July 2026 'in service' reports are taken as misdated.

facilities.name: ICOSNET Oran Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Le Jeune Indépendant (5 July 2026) says ICOSNET, one of the pioneers of the Algerian market, runs two data centres, in Algiers (DZA-006) and Oran, offering cloud computing and offsite backup; status as of that date. Services are stated for the company, not per site. ICOSNET's Oran fact sheet puts the site at Bir El Djir, Oran, with 120 m² (the whole site: server, telecom, power and operations rooms) and a disaster-recovery service; ICOSNET sells colocation (housing) and hosting from its Algiers and Oran data centres, Oran giving geographic redundancy (icosnet.com.dz, July 2025). The fact sheet gives the address as Coopérative Mohammadia, Lot 14, Bir El Djir, with two 100 kVA generators and 2 x 30 kVA modular UPS.

facilities.name: National People's Assembly (APN) Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: APN president Khalida Boufedeche toured the Assembly's data centre on 13 August 2026 and was briefed on its role securing, processing and storing the APN's data (Horizons); status rests on that visit. Holds the legislature's own data. The APN also signed an agreement in June 2026 to use the national sovereign cloud at the CNSN (DZA-001). Inaugurated on 31 October 2024 by then APN president Brahim Boughali, who asked for the remaining phases to be finished for full service (El Massar El Arabi); a delegation received at the APN's seat in Algiers toured it in July 2025.

facilities.name: Diar Dzair Data Centre (El Affroun)
facilities.operator: Sarl Diar Dzair pour le commerce électronique et l'innovation
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: AAPI handed Sarl Diar Dzair a land concession at El Affroun, Blida wilaya, for a data centre on 2 September 2026, expected to create 340 jobs (Algerie Eco); status as of that date. No investment amount, capacity or date given.

facilities.name: Huawei Cloud Cairo Region
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Huawei launched its Cairo cloud region on 21 May 2024 at the Huawei Cloud Summit Egypt, calling it the first public cloud in the region. In June 2026 Huawei Cloud Egypt (CEO Joe Xu) cited NTRA certification, 'Tier 3 licensing' and compliance with Financial Regulatory Authority data-localisation rules. The building hosting the region, and whether Huawei owns it or rents space in a third-party data centre, is not stated. The US$300m is a five-year programme covering services and ecosystem, not the facility's capital cost. Telecom Egypt's release says the region runs in TE's Tier III data centre at Smart Village, connected to EG-IX: this row is a cloud region in rented space, not a Huawei-owned building, and the Tier III is TE's certification, not Huawei's.

facilities.name: Hassan Allam Digital Infrastructure Data Centre
facilities.operator: Hassan Allam Digital Infrastructure and Data Center Solutions
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: NTRA granted Hassan Allam Digital Infrastructure and Data Center Solutions a licence to build and operate a data centre (We Are Tech Africa gives Monday 15 May; iAfrica says June 2026), the tenth data-centre licence in two years. The company is developing it with technology firm A15; investment_usd is the initial first-phase US$400m, with later phases unquantified. The site is not stated. It is to serve government agencies, financial institutions and businesses. A15, a Cairo venture-capital firm, is named as strategic partner, with its equity role unstated. Searched September 2026: no site or opening year announced.

facilities.name: Sénégal Numérique Datacenter ORANA
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: SENUM's 2025 presentation lists ORANA among its three data centres: built 2004, 32 TB storage, 81% utilisation; status rests on that 2025 source. SENUM hosts data for 176 state bodies across its data centres. ORANA is a SENUM site in the Dakar area; the exact location is not stated.

facilities.name: Sénégal Numérique Datacenter Technopole
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: SENUM's 2025 presentation lists Technopole among its three data centres: built 2008, 392 TB storage, 93% utilisation; status rests on that 2025 source. SENUM's head office is at the Technopôle Dakar (Pikine); that the data centre is on the same site is likely but not stated.

facilities.name: Maluana Data Centre (Centro de Dados de Maluana)
facilities.operator: National Science and Technology Park Company (Maluana Science and Technology Park)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: INTIC published (24 July 2025) a commentary calling the Maluana data centre technically capable but under-used, because state institutions have not been mobilised to digitise and move their data to it; status rests on that source. In August 2025 the Ministry of Communications and Digital Transformation signed an MoU with Africa50 to finance a new government data centre in Maputo and the rehabilitation of the Maluana data centre (Club of Mozambique, 14 August 2025). The US Commerce Department (2021) says the government operates Maluana Park's data centre, set to host public administration systems; INTIC (2025) says state institutions have not yet moved their data there. No opening year found. In November 2021 the park's managing company described its newly launched MaluanaBytes cloud computing and storage service, and frequent power cuts at the park (360 Mozambique); the US Trade Administration (December 2021) said Maluana was set to centralise and host the government's public administration systems.

facilities.name: CAMTEL Zamengoe Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: At Zamengoe, Okola subdivision (Centre region), about 30 km from Yaoundé. In use by June 2022, when MINFOPRA's server was hosted there; opening year not stated. CAMTEL calls it Tier III certified and 'the largest in Central Africa' (June 2026); no certifying body is named. Hosted Camtel Cloud Days (December 2025) and visits by Ethio telecom and BEAC's national director (December 2025); operational at Plan International Cameroon's visit on 13 August 2026. Named tenants are public bodies; CAMTEL markets it to businesses too. Built under the NBN II programme with China Exim Bank finance, executed by Huawei Technologies Cameroon with construction by China Shenyang International Cooperation; valued at EUR15m (about US$16.95m at USD1.13/EUR, July 2020), 3,019 m2 site with a 400 m2 server room (floor space is white space), 130 bays and 440 kW of UPS power (ITWeb, July 2020; Journal du Cameroun, May 2023). Uptime's register lists it as Camtel NBN II Data Center; Journal du Cameroun calls the certification Tier III by design. Already operational, with operators renting space, when the telecoms minister visited on 10 July 2020 and told CAMTEL to take full control of it (News Upfront, 11 July 2020). Camtel staff told visiting officers in July 2025 that it plans nine decentralised data centres along its energy distribution points, beside this one (Digital Business Africa); no sites or dates.

facilities.name: Impact Palmarès MINREX Data Centre (Yaoundé)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: L'Economie (8 December 2025): the foreign ministry (MINREX) signed a contract amendment with Impact Palmarès R&D SAS, an Ivorian group, to run secure consular documents (biometric visas, consular cards, laissez-passer); the project includes building a data centre in Yaoundé for sovereign storage of the data. Owner, site, capacity and schedule not stated. The data centre is part of MINREX's Digital Transformation Center (CTDM-MINREX), whose foundation stone was laid in Yaoundé's administrative district in April 2024 under a build-operate-transfer PPP with Impact Palmarès running to at least 2032; the firm promised delivery within 12 months (Biometric Update, 18 April 2024).

facilities.name: CAMPOST Data Centre (Yaoundé)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: CAMIX (7 April 2026) says its Yaoundé PoP is hosted in the CAMPOST data centre, one of its operational sites. DCD (June 2017) lists Campost's data centre as a $52m facility funded by a concessional China Exim Bank loan. Built under the e.post programme, implemented by Huawei, and hosting CAMPOST's applications, colocation, video conferencing and a call centre (CIO Mag, April 2018); in use when the UPU director general visited in July 2016 (DCD). PeeringDB lists the facility on Avenue Konrad Adenauer with CAMIX Yaoundé and three networks (read 21 September 2026). Opening year not found. ST Digital's CEO wrote in June 2025 that CAMPOST's centre has redundancy but single points of failure, closer to Tier II; he runs a competing facility.

facilities.name: Tanzania National Data Centre Dodoma (planned)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology (developer; operator not named)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: One of two national data centres (with Zanzibar) in the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology's budgets: feasibility studies completed in 2024/25 and construction supported in 2025/26 (May 2025); the 2026/27 budget (April 2026) again plans to build it. Parliament's infrastructure committee proposed Sh100bn across the NIDC upgrade and the Dodoma and Zanzibar centres. Status as of April-June 2026. Distinct from eGA's Government Data Centre (TZA-016), which is operating. On 17 March 2026 the minister told Parliament's infrastructure committee that the feasibility study for a large data centre in Dodoma is complete, financing is being agreed with the Ministry of Finance and building should start next financial year: a new build, separate from eGA's operating centre and from the Sh30bn upgrade of NIDC.

facilities.name: Tanzania National Data Centre Zanzibar (planned)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology (developer; operator not named)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: One of two national data centres (with Dodoma) in the Ministry of Communication and Information Technology's budgets: feasibility studies completed in 2024/25 and construction supported in 2025/26 (May 2025); the 2026/27 budget (April 2026) again plans to build it. The records name only Zanzibar, not a site or town. Status as of April-June 2026. ZIBI (November 2025) lists among ZICTIA's upcoming projects a US$75m Tier III data centre of 200 racks and 2 MW, and a US$5m disaster recovery site in Pemba; whether the Tier III centre is this project is not stated. The Revolutionary Government of Zanzibar also signed an MoU with Oman Data Park in October 2022 to build and operate a data centre in Zanzibar.

facilities.name: Amaco Hercules AI Data Centre (Mombasa)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Proposed AI data centre named Hercules, reported by Business Daily (10 September 2026) and TechTrends (15 September 2026); candidate sites Dongo Kundu or Kilindini near Mombasa port. Investment is the proposed project cost, US$1.5 billion as reported (Sh194.2 billion), not a commitment. Independently powered off the grid by GE Vernova gas turbines on an LNG-fuelled power barge under a cooperation agreement with GE; 75-100MW of potential initial data-centre demand is cited, but IT capacity, timeline, financing and tenants are undisclosed.

facilities.name: Kala Data Centre (Lesedi)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Modular high-performance computing data centre at Tlou Energy's Lesedi gas-to-power project, powered by Tlou's gas-fired generation with solar being added; Tlou (ASX/BSE-listed) and UAE-based Kala Data FZCO signed a heads of agreement in March 2025, and Tlou calls it its data centre. First module delivered and commissioning in September 2025 (ITWeb); fully commissioned, with its first full quarter of continuous operation to 30 June 2026 at proof-of-concept revenue (ITWeb, August 2026). Designed for up to 1MW in total; capacity built so far not stated. Tlou announced full commissioning on 19 February 2026; its report for the quarter to 30 June 2026 (31 July 2026) says the data centre is owned and operated by Kala Data and has run a full quarter; neither gives installed capacity or the service model beyond 'computational activities'. Tlou's annual report for the year to 30 June 2026 says the centre ran materially below its design of about 1 MW for lack of gas from the one connected well; a dedicated pipeline from the Lesedi 6 well is being planned, subject to funding, design and approvals, and any expansion depends on gas availability and funding (October 2026).

facilities.name: Mascom Innovation Centre Tier III Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Built for Mascom's own operations and opened to external customers; earns revenue from colocation, cloud, IaaS, disaster recovery, connectivity and managed services (Business Weekly & Review, July 2026). Mascom describes it as internationally certified Tier III and offers government hosting and DR; carrier neutrality is not stated.

facilities.name: Ghana Link Kumasi Tier IV Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Ghana Link's new Kumasi data centre hosts and supports the Integrated Customs Management System (ICUMS) used by the Ghana Revenue Authority's Customs Division; ICUMS systems had been migrated to it by February 2026, when it received ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification from CertiTrust. Ghana Link calls it Tier IV; no certification register in the records confirms that. Dell Technologies is named as a technical partner.

facilities.name: Government of Lesotho Data Centre (Mohale's Hoek)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Communications, Science and Technology (e-Government Infrastructure Project)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Toured by the Communications Minister on 24 May 2018 with only its power station left to build, due within two months; no later source says it opened. Described by the project coordinator as a Tier III data centre (not a certification) that backs up the Ministry of Finance's data centre in Maseru, 100km away, and takes over the Ministry of Communications' Maseru data centre; all government data to be stored across these sites. The African Development Bank published a contract award on 4 October 2021 for consultancy to operationalise the Mohale's Hoek data centre and integrate the three government data centres, so it was not in service then; no later source says it opened. The ICT minister said in October 2026 that the government is upgrading high-performance computing infrastructure at the Mohale's Hoek Data Centre to support AI, scientific modelling and research; the status rests on that statement (Lesotho Times, 23 October 2026).

facilities.name: Project Kobong AI Data Centre (Mokhotlong)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Integrated green-powered AI data centre in the Kobong region of Mokhotlong District, paired with the hydropower plant; the US$6.2bn covers both and is not recorded as investment_usd (M16.38/$1, June 2026). Construction targeted for 2029 after a feasibility study Convalt funds, due around mid-2027. Status from Tech Africa News (3 August 2026) and GroundUp (15 September 2026): still pre-feasibility. Convalt is a portfolio company of ACO Investment Group and expects to seek DFI and project finance. The energy minister said local firms, including Sekhametsi Investment Consortium, would be invited to participate; whether the government takes equity was unanswered in September 2026. DCD (8 June 2026) says further details of the data centre were not disclosed; Convalt is a portfolio company of ACO Investment Group, whose stake is not stated.

facilities.name: UGD Main Data Centre (Tsimbazaza)
facilities.operator: Unité de Gouvernance Digitale (UGD), Presidency of Madagascar (project implementer; operator of the finished site not named)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Fit-out of the right wing, ground floor, of the Ministry of Decentralisation (MID) building at Tsimbazaza, with an energy room in the left wing (PGES, August 2025); coordinates from the PGES. Rehabilitation tendered December 2025 and IT equipment for UGD's data centres (sites A and B) tendered February 2026, both IDA-financed under PRODIGY; which site is which is not stated. Ecofin (24 June 2026): the two PRODIGY data centres, Tsimbazaza and Iavoloha, will host the national digital ID system on renewable power, with construction underway. PRODIGY's US$143M is the whole project, not this facility.

facilities.name: UGD Secondary Data Centre (Iavoloha)
facilities.operator: Unité de Gouvernance Digitale (UGD), Presidency of Madagascar
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Secondary data centre at Iavoloha, south of Antananarivo near the presidential palace (the PGES, August 2025, describes the Andoharanofotsy commune). Air-conditioning tendered August 2025, rehabilitation December 2025 and IT equipment February 2026, all IDA-financed under PRODIGY. Ecofin (24 June 2026): paired with the Tsimbazaza main site to host the national digital ID system on renewable power; construction underway.

facilities.name: LITC KM-4 Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Uptime's register lists KM-4 Data Center, Tripoli, for the Libyan International Telecom Company, with a Tier III design-documents award; the award image is dated 8 July 2024 and marked to expire in 2026. The register does not say the facility is built or in service. LITC's autonomous system AS37791 is registered as 'LITC-TRIP-KM4', naming the KM-4 site as a Tripoli network location of LITC. LITC is an LPTIC subsidiary (LPTIC; CB Insights). It became an Azure ExpressRoute partner in 2021; no source places the on-ramp at KM-4. Searched September 2026: nothing says KM-4 is built or what service model it runs.

facilities.name: Ministry of Education Data Centre (Tripoli)
facilities.operator: Information and Documentation Centre, Ministry of Education
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: LANA (15 April 2026): the Minister of Education, Mohamed Al-Qariou, opened the data centre of the ministry's Information and Documentation Centre in Tripoli and launched the ministry's websites; the centre runs the education data management system, the Taysir data system and the Kawader HR system. The ministry's own report (14 April 2026) calls it the data centre of the Information and Documentation Centre, whose headquarters is on Qurtuba Street, Hay al-Andalus, Tripoli; whether the data centre is in that building is not stated.

facilities.name: Benin National Data Centre (Datacenter national, Abomey-Calavi)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: On Route Nationale Inter-Etats 1 (RNIE1) at Abomey-Calavi. Building handed over in 2019; equipment installed over nine months and first technical tests begun 1 June 2021 under the ASSI, with ANSI/TIA-942 rated-3 certification then in progress, dual fibre connection (numerique.gouv.bj, 1 Jun 2021). Built under the Programme de renforcement des structures centrales de gouvernance (PRSCG). Listed as in operation in February 2026 and cited by ASIN's director general in June 2026. DCD (March 2026) gives 300 sqm without saying whether that is white space, and names SBIM as operator. The ministry commissioned a World Bank-funded (WARDIP) feasibility study in 2026 for a second, redundant national data centre, possibly elsewhere in West Africa; the national AI and big data strategy aims to add AI capability here. TIA's register shows ANSI/TIA-942-B Rated-3 Design certification for ASSI's CDN 1 at Zogbadjè, Abomey-Calavi (Domaine ORTB), issued by EPI in February 2019 and expired August 2021; no later award found. SBIN was placed under delegated management by Sonatel in May 2021 (Wikipedia). The second phase of the World Bank's West Africa regional digital programme (approved 2026-03-11) funds a redundancy site for this national data centre at US$6.0m within Benin's EUR 51.1m credit; no site, capacity or delivery date is stated.

facilities.name: Greenline Grand Parakou Data Facility
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Greenline Technologies signed definitive agreements on 7 August 2025 for the Grand Parakou project, a 10 MW solar PV plant with a Tier III-ready data facility; Greenline is EPC contractor and long-term O&M operator, construction starts on Notice to Proceed and commissioning is targeted for 2026 (Greenline, Aug 2025). The counterparties and the facility's owner are not named. Carrier neutrality is as designed, not yet in service.

facilities.name: Ministry of Economy and Finance Data Centre (MEF Benin)
facilities.operator: Ministère de l'Economie et des Finances (MEF)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Known from BOAD's IATI record of a XOF 19.5bn loan (two tranches value-dated 19 May 2026) whose first object is 'la modernisation et la mise en redondance du Data Center du Ministère de l'Economie et des Finances'. The loan also covers two other systems, so no share of it is attributed to the data centre and investment_usd is left blank.

facilities.name: E²C Data Centre (Brazzaville)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The energy minister visited construction of E²C's data centre, alongside its new digitised archive centre, on 12 September 2025 (ADIAC, 13 Sep 2025); he said it would host the data of E²C and of other operators. The visit was to installations in E²C's direction building (La Semaine Africaine), and E²C's head office is in Brazzaville (e2c.cg).

facilities.name: Congo Télécom Data Centre Brazzaville
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Congo Télécom's deputy DG said in August 2026 that the operator has data centres able to host data in Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire and Oyo (La Semaine Africaine, 20 Aug 2026); status rests on that statement. No capacity or site details are given. Congo Télécom's site lists no hosting or colocation product, so whether the centres are captive or rented is not known.

facilities.name: Congo Télécom Data Centre Pointe-Noire
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Congo Télécom's deputy DG said in August 2026 that the operator has data centres able to host data in Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire and Oyo (La Semaine Africaine, 20 Aug 2026); status rests on that statement. Distinct from ARPCE's Pointe-Noire data centre (COG-002). No capacity or site details are given. Congo Télécom's site lists no hosting or colocation product, so whether the centres are captive or rented is not known.

facilities.name: Congo Télécom Data Centre Oyo
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Congo Télécom's deputy DG said in August 2026 that the operator has data centres able to host data in Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire and Oyo, Cuvette department (La Semaine Africaine, 20 Aug 2026); status rests on that statement. No capacity or site details are given. Congo Télécom's site lists no hosting or colocation product, so whether the centres are captive or rented is not known.

facilities.name: Djibouti Telecom Ras Dika CLS and Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The World Bank Group's Country Private Sector Diagnostic (September 2026, market data as of July 2025) says Djibouti Telecom is completing a new data centre in the Ras Dika area of the capital that will also serve as the landing point for the 2Africa cable. Djibouti Telecom announced the Ras Dika CLS fully operational on 7 August 2023 (Submarine Networks), and its colocation page offers colocation in the Ras-Dika building; the year is the CLS's. Djibouti Telecom describes a three-floor building with a 250 sqm equipment room on each floor, the third floor a dedicated colocation centre. Floor space is the design figure from Djibouti Telecom's October 2021 announcement: three floors, each with a 250 m2 equipment room, the third reserved for neutral colocation aimed at cloud providers; the page's update lists PEACE, 2Africa, Africa-1, SMW6 and IEX as hosted at Ras Dika.

facilities.name: Horus Labs AI Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: RURA granted Horus Labs Ltd an Application Service Provider - Data Centre Tier III licence to build and operate an AI data centre offering GPU computing, AI cloud and colocation; the licence text carries no date and was filed April 2026. Xalam's January 2026 brief lists Horus Labs as a small-scale, locally focused projected GPU cluster. Neither source gives a site, capacity or opening date. Horus Labs' website (read September 2026) says it is 'heads-down working on our flagship AI data center in Rwanda' and gives no site, capacity or date.

facilities.name: TNM Limbe Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: In Limbe, Blantyre. TNM calls it its existing data centre (ITWeb, 11 September 2026) and plans to integrate it with the Kanengo data centre it bought from OCL (MWI-003) into one cloud platform. Capacity, year and services not stated. TNM's CTO called Kanengo a replica of the Blantyre facility's power, cooling and servers (Times, 11 September 2026); no source says whether Limbe hosts outside customers or when it opened.

facilities.name: Sparc Systems Data Centre Lilongwe
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Launched in Lilongwe at Sparc's Think Tech Thursday event (reported 1 May 2026) to offer local hosting as an alternative to offshore hosting. Sparc says it can host up to 120 racks. Sparc Systems operates in Malawi, Zambia, Tanzania, Mozambique and Rwanda. Sparc's notice places the data centre at its Lilongwe headquarters offices and names financial institutions, telecoms networks, government and SMEs as the clients it targets.

facilities.name: Zimbabwe Centre for High Performance Computing (University of Zimbabwe)
facilities.operator: Zimbabwe Centre for High Performance Computing (ZCHPC), University of Zimbabwe
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Supercomputer built by Inspur Group (with Dameng) and handed over to the University of Zimbabwe on 6 February 2015; Phase 2 aimed to raise capacity from 36 to over 300 teraflops and add cloud services. investment_usd is the Phase 2 grant only, AidData's conversion of RMB 100M. AidData also says the Phase 1 loan was not disbursed as planned, although the project was handed over. Status rests on Techzim (April 2026), which says access is quoted at tens of thousands of dollars, and the ICT minister naming the centre as national infrastructure (July 2026). President Mnangagwa commissioned Phase 2 at the Zimbabwe Science Park complex, University of Zimbabwe, on 15 August 2025, about 15 times faster than Phase 1; the Ministry of Health's Impilo electronic health records and the civil registry run on it (developzim; Business Daily, August 2025).

facilities.name: Econet Wireless Zimbabwe Harare Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Newly commissioned, onboarding corporate clients from end of June 2025 (Mbare Times, 7 June 2025); developed with Africa Data Centres, a sister company; Econet plans to double it to 10MW. The 5MW is as reported, not stated to be IT load. The ICT minister named Econet's AI Data Centre as national infrastructure in July 2026, which is the newest status source; Econet's own GPU compute is at the Cassava AI Factory in South Africa. The Econet Data Centre (EDC) is owned by Econet Wireless Zimbabwe and is in Willowvale, Harare; ADC helped design and build it (NewsDay, 5 June 2025), and Genesisoft (April 2026) lists it separately from ADC Harare, so it is a distinct facility from ZWE-001. Econet's notice of 24 December 2025 moved all the Group's real estate and passive infrastructure into Econet InfraCo, 70% held by the Group after March 2026, with ownership and control unchanged; it does not name the data centre.

facilities.name: Zimbabwe National Data Centre
facilities.operator: Ministry of ICT, Postal and Courier Services
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Commissioned in Harare in 2021 with Chinese government assistance, built by Inspur Group and Sino-Zimbabwe (This is Africa, September 2026); Xalam (July 2025) calls it Huawei-built. The 2027 Budget Strategy Paper (30 July 2026) plans a Tier IV upgrade, a geographically separate disaster-recovery site and an expanded Smart Government Private Cloud for MDAs, with HPC capacity for AI; the minister announced the Tier IV plan in 2025. Commissioned on 24 February 2021 at the Mukwati government complex, Harare, by the ICT ministry with the Office of the President and Cabinet (TechnoMag); no source found says whether China's assistance was a grant or a loan. In January 2025 the ICT minister said a site had been found for a new Tier IV centre, with completion targeted for end-2025 (The Herald, 25 January 2025). In November 2025 she said the national data centre expansion and a new city data centre had stalled for lack of funds, the ministry having received ZWG644M against a ZWG10.7bn bid (The Herald, 7 November 2025). In February 2026 she said government was building a new data centre in Harare with a disaster-recovery site in Bulawayo (Newsreel Zimbabwe, 8 February 2026).

facilities.name: Cable Consortium of Liberia Monrovia Landing Station
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: CCL advertises rack colocation in its Monrovia landing facility: 2-10U up to 2 kW, half rack 3 kW, full 42U rack 5 kW, with UPS and diesel backup, HVAC, fire suppression, CCTV and biometric access (CCL site, April 2025); status rests on that page. The ACE cable lands at the Monrovia Cable Landing Station in central Monrovia (MoPT WARDIP ESMF, December 2025).

facilities.name: Liberia E-Government Data Centre (Cybastion Digital Fast Track)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Under a five-year master service framework agreement signed with the Government of Liberia on 23 September 2024, US-based Cybastion (spelt Cybaston by MICAT) is to design, build and implement a scalable data centre hosting existing and future e-government services, handing its digital capabilities to the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications in September 2029 (MICAT). In July 2026 the Posts and Telecommunications minister still listed a national data centre among undated plans, naming no builder or site (ELBC). In September 2026 the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications presented a planned national data centre to investors at an investment dialogue in New York; one investor had expressed interest, but the minister said the investment model and site were undecided pending technical and feasibility studies, and participants raised reliable power supply as the main constraint (Ecofin Agency, 30 September 2026). Cybastion was not named.

facilities.name: National Transit Authority Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: NTA's managing director said construction of a dedicated NTA data centre was under way, to support an electronic revenue-payment system contracted to Labora, a Liberian-owned company, for US$248,000 (Liberia Excellent News, 19 August 2026). Site and size not stated.

facilities.name: Central Bank of Liberia Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: CBL's deputy governor for operations said the bank is developing a new CBL-owned data centre to host and manage critical national payment infrastructure, alongside the RTGS, ACH and the planned Liberia Interbank Payment and Settlement Systems (Liberian Observer, 25 August 2026). Site, size and date not stated. In November 2025 CBL sought an owner's engineer to design and supervise construction of a new head office and purpose-built facility housing LIB-PSS operations with secure ICT spaces (CBL REOI, closing 1 December 2025); no construction contract reported by September 2026, so Planned stands. Distinct from CBL's existing main and recovery data centres, upgraded with a 2023 African Development Fund grant (separate row).

facilities.name: Virtual Space Data Centre (Airbus / NUST)
facilities.operator: Namibia University of Science and Technology (NUST), with Airbus
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: ITWeb (15 June 2026) lists it among Namibia's established commercial data centres, as a collaboration run by Airbus and NUST. Nothing else about it is in the records. Set up under a letter of intent signed by NUST and Airbus Defence and Space on 16 February 2017, in Windhoek, to receive imagery from Airbus's SPOT, Pleiades and TerraSAR-X satellites and build a geo-intelligence database for government ministries (New Era).

facilities.name: Sudan National Data Centre, Port Sudan (alternative site)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Digital Transformation and Communications
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The Minister of Digital Transformation and Communications listed a national data centre in Port Sudan, as an alternative to the Khartoum state data centre, among the ministry's future projects (press conference of 31 January 2026, Official Spokesperson Platform). No date, size or budget given. On 15 March 2026 the minister still described the alternative national data centre as a project, one of the largest current investments in technical infrastructure (Nabd Sudan).

facilities.name: QGroup House Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: In QGroup House, the group's eight-storey headquarters on Kairaba Avenue (Kanifing), inaugurated by President Barrow on 29 April 2026 (State House, The Point; DCD, 5 May 2026). QGroup calls it the country's first data centre; size and capacity not disclosed. QGroup includes QCell, Quantum Net, AGIB Bank and Espace Motors. A Huawei Africa vice-president spoke at the launch and recalled Huawei's work with QCell; no source says Huawei supplied this facility. Not the Gamtel Kairaba exchange (GMB-001). Foroyaa (30 April 2026) calls it the QD Center; neither QGroup nor the State House states its service model, size or supplier.

facilities.name: Gambia National Data Centre (Abuko)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Inaugurated by President Barrow on 30 June 2026 with the NIMS digital ID launch (The Standard, 1 July 2026; Biometric Update, 3 July 2026). Built and operated by MIDSA, a subsidiary of Ghana's Margins ID Group, under a BOT contract awarded January 2026; Margins' CEO calls it sovereign infrastructure owned by the people of The Gambia and says it is ISO-certified. Margins describes the contract as design, build, finance, co-operate and transfer; the term and transfer date are not published. Citi Newsroom (July 2026) says the identity database is owned by the State.

facilities.name: Niger National Data Centre (DTS/FO Tier III, Niamey)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Communication and New Information Technologies (DTS/FO project unit)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Second component of Niger's Trans-Sahara Optical Fibre Backbone (DTS/FO) project, alongside 1,031 km of fibre and an 88 km Niamey loop to connect administrative sites to it. In March 2025 the minister put it at 13% executed, built with AfDB support for 9.5bn FCFA (converted at ~607 XOF/USD, March 2025, ~US$15.65m; the data-centre component only), with handover expected by 30 September 2025. At the fibre handover on 14 November 2025 the building was built but the data centre not yet commissioned (ANP; AfDB calls it the 'future national data centre'); status rests on that date. Whole project estimated at EUR 43m (AfDB). Sofrecom's feasibility study specified Tier III+, for government applications with part of the space sold as hosting to businesses. Site at PK5, Lazaret quarter, Arrondissement Communal Niamey II, on a 2,300 m² building footprint with a government zone and a commercial zone (ESIA, 2022). Works by CGPS-SA and LORYNE (Burkina Faso) began in 2022, were interrupted, and stood at 85% in June 2025 with equipment still on order (Le Sahel, ANP). Oceans News (21 November 2025) reports the data centre's installations nearing completion, with full service after final technical tests; no commissioning reported since. ANSI's director-general inspected the works on 29 October 2026 and found the centre still under construction, without giving a completion date (ANSI); status as of that date.

facilities.name: UBOS Statistics House Data Centre (Entebbe)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Ground broken August 2026 on the Statistics House Entebbe office block (four floors and three basements, UGX 76bn), which is to hold a UBOS data processing centre alongside a data science hub, innovation hub, training centre and offices; ROKO Construction is the contractor and is to finish within three years. No data-centre capacity published.

facilities.name: ACE Gabon Carrier Hotel (Gabon Datacenter)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Tier III carrier hotel ('Carrier Hotel neutre') under construction by ACE Gabon SA; on a site visit reported 31 July 2026 the minister gave delivery for late November to early December 2026. Planned 160 racks and more than 1 MW of electrical power; to be interconnected with the submarine cables serving Gabon. The minister said it is a public structure financed by the local banking sector, distinct from ST Digital's private Nkok data centre (GAB-001). Cyriaque Didier Koma is named director general of Gabon Datacenter. Location not stated. Neither the July 2026 reports nor ACE Gabon's owner SPIN give the site; ACE Gabon's cable landing station is in Libreville.

facilities.name: CNIAPGE Government Data Centre
facilities.operator: CNIAPGE (Centro Nacional para la Informatización de la Administración Pública de Guinea Ecuatorial)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The core of the state's e-government project: a data centre was set up in the project's first phase, completed in January 2019 (Oficina de Información y Prensa). In April 2025 CNIAPGE told its board the centre's active and passive equipment needed renewing, to be done gradually (Oficina de Información y Prensa, 15 April 2025). BTW Media (August 2025) says CNIAPGE runs a Tier III data centre and a private government network with 40 GB bandwidth; no certification is cited. CNIAPGE signed a Microsoft licence agreement in June 2015, a software licence rather than a hyperscaler relationship. Status as of April 2025. CNIAPGE's 2024 plan lists fitting out a building to house the state's information, the data centre, as one of its own objectives, and records a debt to GITGE as a supplier: a CNIAPGE site, not GITGE's Sipopo Datacenter (GNQ-001). Guinea Info Market (June 2017) already lists CNIAPGE as running a Tier III data centre, at its Malabo II address; the opening year is not given, and no Uptime award is cited. CNIAPGE's director general (A&A Capital, May 2022) dates its operations from 2015, after it was created by decree in 2013, and counts a data centre among its achievements alongside 14 connected institutions on a 12 km private government network; its services then covered Malabo only.

facilities.name: Somaliland Government Data and Cybersecurity Center
facilities.operator: Somaliland Ministry of Information and Communication Technology (MICT)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Groundbreaking on 22 September 2025 at the MICT in Hargeisa (TaiwanICDF, 20 October 2025). Described as Somaliland's first government data centre: main building, server facilities and cybersecurity management systems, part of its National Data Center Project with the S-Road e-government system. Somaliland is unrecognised territory, recorded under SOM as SOM-003 is. Status as of October 2025.

facilities.name: Golis Telecom Birta Dheer Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: At Birta Dheer, near Garowe (Puntland). A Golis Telecom electrical engineer reported in January 2026 that the site's earthing grid had been installed and tested (LinkedIn, 21 January 2026); capacity, opening date and service model are not stated. Status as of January 2026.

facilities.name: Government Online Centre (GOC)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Information Technology, Communication and Innovation (MITCI)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The government's own data centre at Ebene, formally opened in May 2005, grown from five server racks to about 80 and run 24/7 (L'Express, 31 December 2025). MITCI calls it Tier III compliant and implementing ISO 27001 (September 2025), with Mauritius Telecom's Tier IV site at Rose-Belle (MUS-001) as its secondary site. MITCI procured a SAN and backup system for the GOC and its DR site (awarded early 2026) and a scale-out storage system (awarded to Blanche Birger Co. Ltd, March 2026). The MSB's ISO 27001 register at 31 December 2025 does not list the GOC. A MITCI bid evaluation (2025) says the GOC has acquired a Tier IV data centre at Rose-Belle as its disaster-recovery site and is considering running it active-active with the main site; the networking equipment for it went to Network & Security Consulting Ltd for Rs 27.55M excluding VAT.

facilities.name: Aphelion DC3
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Telecom Review Africa (16 July 2025) lists Aphelion DC3 in Port Louis among ten data centres operating in Mauritius, with multiple redundant backbone connections to the public IP network. No other detail. DatacenterMap lists it as Aphelion Limited's ADC3 at Noah Wealth Center, JinFei Smart City, Terre Rouge, north of Port Louis (read September 2026).

facilities.name: Harel Mallac Technologies Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Telecom Review Africa (16 July 2025) lists it in Port Louis among ten data centres operating in Mauritius and calls it a Tier III data centre with fibre and radio access; no certificate is cited. DatacenterMap gives the address as 18 Edith Cavell Street, Port Louis (read September 2026).

facilities.name: Rogers Capital Les Cascades Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Telecom Review Africa (16 July 2025) lists it in Port Louis as a high-availability site with its own infrastructure, allowing a 50-50 load-balanced configuration, separately from Rogers Capital's La Tour Koenig (MUS-004) and Ebene (MUS-003) sites. DatacenterMap lists it at Les Cascades Building, Edith Cavell Street, Port Louis, and lists a separate 'Rogers Capital Port Louis Data Center' at 59 Mere Barthelemy Street; Rogers Capital's own services page names only Ebene (MUS-003) and La Tour Koenig (MUS-004), so both Port Louis listings may be retired sites. Searches in September 2026 found no current Rogers Capital statement that Les Cascades operates; its services page names only Ebene and La Tour Koenig, and only a directory ascribes the site to Rogers Capital Technology Services.

facilities.name: Bhumishq Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Bhumishq's Cybercity Data Centre in the MINDSPACE building, Ebene Cybercity: 500 sqm of server space (Prodesign; Bramston, March 2025, which also gives 80 racks), built 2006-2010 for Rs 260 million as part of the Bhumi Fund's MINDSPACE project. Uptime lists a Tier IV Certification of Design Documents; no constructed-facility award is listed. Telecom Review Africa (16 July 2025) places it at Reduit and calls it carrier-neutral. Bhumishq's own site (read September 2026) names Bhumishq Technologies Ltd, 80 racks and a Tier IV design certification; Uptime lists the award under Bhumishq Teleserve Ltd.

facilities.name: Birger Candos Recovery Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Telecom Review Africa (16 July 2025) lists the BIRGER Candos Recovery Center in Quatre Bornes among ten data centres operating in Mauritius, with redundant precision cooling. Birger's own page (read September 2026) places its recovery centre at its Technology Operation Centre in Phoenix, and a directory ascribes a Candos Recovery Centre in Quatre Bornes to Continuity Mauritius Co. Ltd (shareholders Mauritius Telecom, Blanche Birger and ContinuitySA); no source reconciles the two.

facilities.name: Chad National Data Centre Secondary Site (Farcha)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: ATPE (1 June 2023) reports the telecoms minister visiting the secondary data centre at Farcha, 90% built, alongside the main centre at Klemat (TCD-001), both under the China EXIM-financed PMICE. In August 2026 the minister announced two data centres commissioned at N'Djamena, which may be these two. On 7 August 2026 the minister told the CESCE that two data centres were in service at N'Djamena, without naming them (Tachad); the security audit and certification of the main centre were still pending in May 2026. No source names the Farcha site's operator.

facilities.name: Tigo Chad Data Centre N'Djamena (Flexenclosure, 2016)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: DCD (6 January 2026) says Chad's first data centre was developed in 2016: a 374 m2 (4,025 sq ft) prefabricated facility built in Sweden by Flexenclosure, shipped to N'Djamena, designed for 400 kW of IT load, costing $6 million at the time. It names no owner or operator. Commissioned by Millicom for Tigo Chad and inaugurated 21 June 2016 (Osiris); 126 racks and close to 1 MW total load (Millicom). Maroc Telecom completed its purchase of 100% of Tigo Chad on 27 June 2019 and renamed it Moov Africa Tchad from January 2021; no source says whether the 2016 container data centre still runs.

facilities.name: Sierra Leone National Data Centre (NatCA Tower)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Housed in the 10-storey NatCA headquarters at Southridge, Freetown, which also holds MoCTI and a network operations centre; construction began in 2015 and President Bio commissioned it in April 2026 (SLENA, 17 April 2026). MoCTI showed the UN the 'Government Data Centre at NatCA Tower' in September 2026 and outlined plans for a redundancy site at State House (Sierra Loaded, 5 September 2026). No capacity, tier or vendor figures published.

facilities.name: Trinity Technologies Datacenter (Hai Malakal)
facilities.operator: Trinity Technologies Limited (ISP services through its subsidiary Spazio Tech Solutions Ltd)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The company's own site (accessed 29 August 2026) advertises colocation and hosting in 'our Tier 2 Datacenter' in Hai Malakal, Juba; Tier 2 is self-described, with no certification named. Operating status rests on that page alone. No capacity, floor space or year given. Commissioned on 28 May 2019 at the Trinity Technologies Centre by the NCA's director general, as a Tier II colocation facility hosting the m-GURUSH mobile money platform (Xinhua, Aptantech).

facilities.name: SETIC Government Data Centre
facilities.operator: Secrétariat Exécutif des Technologies de l'Information et de la Communication (SETIC), Ministry of Finance, Budget and Digital Economy
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The national AI strategy validated in April 2026 plans to modernise 'the data center of SETIC' alongside a sovereign cloud (Iwacu, April 2026); status taken as Operational because the strategy modernises an existing centre. PAFEN re-tendered virtualisation and backup equipment and licences for SETIC on 7 April 2026. No capacity, site or vendor published. Participants at the national data governance strategy workshop (UNECA, April 2025) list a 'mini data center national' in operation at SETIC. The national data centre PAFEN provides for is not yet a facility: SETIC was still recruiting consultants for a study of government data hosting, and the World Bank's March 2026 mid-term review names it only as a priority, with no site or builder. Iwacu (4 May 2021) already describes SETIC as running a data centre that hosts the sites and data of state institutions free of charge; ministries' IT focal points questioned its security, and many ministries still hosted their sites on servers abroad.

facilities.name: São Tomé and Príncipe Government Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: A World Bank mission (8–12 September 2025) reports a consultancy's assessment of the existing government data centre, which it rates high-risk because it sits at sea level. Options: requalify it (~EUR 0.5M), build a new Tier III centre (~EUR 4.6M), or a hybrid with cloud; the consultancy recommends migrating government systems to a new centre or to cloud controlled by INIC, and the system integrator recommends cloud hosting for digital ID. No decision recorded. INIC runs the data centre, set up with Brazil's SERPRO in 2008, and offers hosting from it to public bodies and private clients; INIC's address is the Prime Minister's office building in São Tomé city (INIC; Digital Governance Strategy, January 2020). The World Bank-funded assessment of a disaster-resilient site for a new centre, with a disaster-recovery and transition plan, was awarded to Grupo Erre of Braga, Portugal (Braga TV, 12 March 2025).

facilities.name: AGETIC Government Data Centre
facilities.operator: AGETIC (Agence des technologies de l'information et de la communication)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: ITU's 2022 PKI framework for Mali names two government data centres, SMTD's and AGETIC's. AGETIC's offers the administration IaaS, SaaS and backup; power is not redundant except the UPS; it has a DR site with real-time replication; access by biometrics and badge, CCTV, armoured doors and guards. Status rests on that 2022 report. Not the 2026 National Data Centre (MLI-001), which the row attributes to SMTD. AGETIC is based at the Bibliothèque Nationale, ACI 2000, Bamako; its live site (read 21 September 2026) says its teams watch the state's critical systems 24/7, and its 2026 procurement plan budgets room fit-out, IT, power and cooling equipment.

facilities.name: Benin Presidency Government Data Centre
facilities.operator: Presidency of the Republic of Benin
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: ECOWAS's SIGTEL regional infrastructure page lists two government-owned data centres in Benin, at the Presidency and the Ministry of Finance in Cotonou; the page is undated and gives no size, status or operator.

facilities.name: Comoros National Data Centre (PADEC, Universite des Comores campus)
facilities.operator: ANADEN (National Agency for Digital Development), implementing agency; PPP operator to be recruited
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The IsDB general procurement notice for ANADEN's e-government project (12 March 2026) lists, under Component A financed entirely by the AfDB, the supply of equipment and the construction and commissioning of a national data centre, an incubator and an information centre on the Universite des Comores campus in Moroni. The AfDB approved EUR 9.51M for PADEC in October 2024 to build a new data centre and operationalise the existing secondary one, with a PPP operator to run them; the 2025 work plan (March 2025) includes creating the data centre. Distinct from COM-001, the public administration data centre inaugurated in May 2025, which is not described as on the university campus. A separate site from COM-001: the AfDB procurement plan covers the construction of a new main data centre and the upgrading of the existing secondary one, and COM-001 is an existing RCIP-4 facility returned to service and inaugurated in May 2025.

facilities.name: Eritel Asmara
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Eritel's Private Cloud Services page (retrieved 31 August 2026) says its Nextcloud private cloud is hosted entirely in Eritel's own datacentres, plural, with a 90% availability commitment and a recovery time objective of up to six days; status rests on that page. It names no site, capacity or owner: this row stands for Eritel's datacentres until a source separates them, and Asmara is taken from the service's per-site connectivity terms, not stated as the location.

facilities.name: TechPark CV Data Center II (DC2, Praia Campus)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The AfDB's Phase II appraisal (October 2022) lists three data centres at the park: DC1, the first government-owned data centre in Praia (CPV-001); DC2, financed by the AfDB under Phase I, in Praia and to be managed through a PPP concession; and DC3, the government-run disaster-recovery site (CPV-002). The park's main site is at Achada Grande Frente, Praia. TechPark CV was inaugurated on 5 May 2025, and the AfDB says it includes a fully equipped data centre; whether DC2 is in service and who holds the concession is not stated. DCD (2023) reported that Phase II would furnish two data centres under a PPP. TechPark CV's chairman, Carlos Monteiro, said at the May 2025 inauguration that the park has the existing NOSi-run public data centre and the Mindelo disaster-recovery mirror, and will have a third data centre in Praia to be handed to private management (Voz do Arquipélago). The Phase II ESIA (August 2022) aims for DC2 to be commercial under a concession agreement, partly equipped under Phase II.

facilities.name: NPS Primary Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The National Police Service's primary data centre in Nairobi, holding an Uptime Institute Tier III Design Documents certification (date not shown). NPS says the data centre is the receiving and recording point for CCTV images feeding its Integrated Command, Control and Communication (IC3) centre. Location within Nairobi not published. The IC3 command centre it serves has run since May 2015 (Capital FM, May 2018); no source gives the data centre's own opening year.

facilities.name: SEACOM Mombasa Cable Landing Station
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: SEACOM's landing station for its cable at Mombasa Old Town (Swahili Cultural Centre, Mvita Road, per PeeringDB and Colo Map; Inflect gives Sir Mbarak Hinawy Road). Registered in PeeringDB with about 30 networks (Lineserve, July 2026), including Google (AS15169); Inflect lists cabinet colocation. Ownership follows SEACOM's group chain, as on its other landing-station rows.

facilities.name: National Data Recovery Centre (Naivasha)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Government backup data centre in Naivasha begun by the National Treasury in 2009 (contractor Misort Africa Ltd, Sh782M over 96 weeks, due December 2014). About 68% complete and unused after roughly Sh1.1bn of phases one and two was paid; equipment worth over Sh100M stolen or vandalised; cost estimates now exceed Sh5bn. Transferred to the ICT ministry, which says it wants to revive and complete it (Auditor-General's 2023/24 report, as reported March 2025). The Auditor-General's 2023/24 report itself: the National Treasury contracted the centre in 2009 for Kshs 782.8M; phases I (Kshs 899.6M) and II (Kshs 205.3M) were completed and paid; a dispute over phase III ended in an arbitration award to the contractor of Kshs 4.10bn, which with interest stood at Kshs 5.55bn at 30 June 2024; the project remains unused.

facilities.name: MRTAM Government Data Centre (ARTEC, Andohatapenaka)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Digital Development, Posts and Telecommunications (MNDPT)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The state's first data centre, built by Huawei under the MRTAM project to modernise the administration's telecoms network (fibre, LTE, CCTV and a data centre), financed by a USD 47.2M China Exim Bank loan approved in 2020 (Ecofin); the loan covers the whole programme. In March 2021 the minister said it would sit in ARTEC's compound at Andohatapenaka and that the equipment had reached Toamasina (2424.mg); in 2022 technicians were being trained to run it, and equipment handovers under MRTAM were under way in December 2022. No source reports its commissioning. In March 2022 the digital minister said Huawei was still working with the ministry to set up the state's first data centre, which would host all e-government applications, and about forty Malagasy technicians were being trained to run it (2424.mg); a December 2022 handover of MRTAM security equipment again listed the data centre among the project's components without saying it was in service (TeamGasy).

facilities.name: MCB Pailles Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Uptime lists Tier III Certification of Design Documents and of Constructed Facility for The Mauritius Commercial Bank's Pailles Data Centre; Bramston & Associates (March 2025) describes it as the bank's Tier III certified data centre safeguarding its critical banking systems.

facilities.name: Kaldera Data Center (Ebene Mews)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: PeeringDB lists Kaldera's facility at 57 Cybercity (Ebene Mews), 3rd floor, Ebene. Kaldera, a licensed Mauritian ISP (AS37722), says it runs three data centres offering housing and co-location, managed hosting and cloud, with peering to MIXP; this row is the PeeringDB-listed site, and the other two are not located.

facilities.name: Government Integrated Data Center (MInT)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The ministry's existing data centre, which hosts government networks and serves public bodies, universities, telcos and banks (DCD and Addis Fortune, September 2020); MInT's February 2023 e-government assessment calls it the Government Integrated Data Center and recommends assessing it before upgrades. Status as of February 2023. Distinct from the ICT Park national data centre (ETH-010).

facilities.name: Ethio Telecom Nefas Silk Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: On Uptime Institute's register with Tier III Certification of Design Documents (checked September 2026), listed as a separate site from Ethio Telecom's Old Airport, Tikur Anbessa and Debre Birhan facilities. Ethio Telecom reported 5MW of Tier III-certified capacity across six facilities in its 2025/26 results (July 2026), without naming them; no source states this site is in service.

facilities.name: Ethio Telecom Old Airport Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: On Uptime Institute's register with Tier III Certification of Design Documents (checked September 2026), listed as a separate site from Ethio Telecom's Nefas Silk, Tikur Anbessa and Debre Birhan facilities. Ethio Telecom reported 5MW of Tier III-certified capacity across six facilities in its 2025/26 results (July 2026), without naming them; no source states this site is in service.

facilities.name: Ethio Telecom Tikur Anbessa Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: On Uptime Institute's register with Tier III Certification of Design Documents, issued January 2025 and valid to 2027 (checked September 2026), listed as a separate site from Ethio Telecom's Nefas Silk, Old Airport and Debre Birhan facilities. Ethio Telecom reported 5MW of Tier III-certified capacity across six facilities in its 2025/26 results (July 2026), without naming them; no source states this site is in service.

facilities.name: Ethio Telecom Debre Birhan Data Center DC01
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: In the Ethio Telecom Building, Nig Eleni Kebele, Debre Birhan, about 120km north-east of Addis Ababa; on Uptime Institute's register with Tier III Certification of Design Documents (October 2025) and listed in the location annex of Ethio Telecom's ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Telecloud certificate (Datacenters.com). Ethio Telecom reported six Tier III facilities with a dual-site architecture 120km apart (July 2026); status rests on that report.

facilities.name: CBE-FI Data Center, Phase 1
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The Commercial Bank of Ethiopia's data centre project in Debre Berhan, on Uptime Institute's register with Tier IV Certification of Design Documents (checked September 2026). No source states whether it has been built.

facilities.name: Zemen Bank Data Center (ZBDCF01)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: On Uptime Institute's register as ZBDCF01 with Tier III Certification of Design Documents (checked September 2026). Zemen Bank's website (retrieved September 2026) says the bank operates with a Tier III certified data centre; status rests on that page.

facilities.name: Geek Zone Data Center PLC (Holeta)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: A bitcoin mining farm in the Holeta area of Oromia, powered on in January 2024 under a supply agreement with the national grid, with 70MW of its first phase in operation on 30,000 sqm of land within a 500MW mining farm; the 70MW is farm load, not IT load. Listed on Bitdeer's hosting marketplace as a site not affiliated with Bitdeer; distinct from Bitdeer's own Oromia site (ETH-007). Owner not disclosed. Ethiopian Electric Power cut deliveries to bitcoin miners to 23% of contracted levels by September 2026 (BitKE, 18 September 2026), curtailing rather than disconnecting them.

facilities.name: Wingu Africa Data Center Berbera
facilities.operator: Wingu Africa Data Center PLC (Wingu Africa Group)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Batalaale Beach, Zone 20, Berbera, Somaliland (recorded under SOM as SOM-004 is). Wingu announced the first phase commissioned on 13 February and ready for service on 27 February 2022 (the release says 2021, which its date contradicts); Somaliland's first carrier-neutral data centre. It hosts the PEACE cable for the local landing party. Coordinates from PeeringDB.

facilities.name: Dalkom Somalia Mogadishu Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Dalkom House, AMISOM Compound, Airport Road, Mogadishu. The operator advertises carrier-grade colocation in its Mogadishu data centre, with others in Nairobi and Mombasa, connected to its international gateways; PeeringDB lists its Dalkom CLS at that address (updated September 2025). Status rests on its website (retrieved September 2026) and that entry.

facilities.name: South Sudan National Data Centre (MICT&PS)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Information, Communication Technology and Postal Services
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The ministry announced in October 2024 that it would build the country's first resilient data centre, with World Bank resources, to host public- and private-sector data. The government spokesman said on 30 April 2026 that the national data centre was halfway built. Status as of April 2026. Distinct from the MGI-managed gateway data centre (SSD-001).

facilities.name: Vodacom Mozambique Maputo Rooftop Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Flexenclosure eCentre of three 42 sqm prefabricated modules on the helipad of a six-storey building in central Maputo, finished in May 2013 in eight days as Vodacom Mozambique's disaster recovery centre for mission-critical data and telecom equipment (IT News Africa, May 2013; STULZ project page, 174 kW cooling). Floor space is the modules' total. Distinct from the 500 sqm eCentre switching centre in Matola (MOZ-004). No source after 2014 says whether it is still in use. DCD (September 2013) places the modules on the helipad of Vodacom's regional office in central Maputo; no source after 2014 was found on whether it still runs.

facilities.name: NetOne NDC1
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: NetOne markets NDC1 as a purpose-built data centre with 'fault-tolerant Tier III certification', presence of major telcos, per-rack 3 kVA online UPS and generator backup; no Uptime Institute record was checked. Location is given only as NetOne's corporate office, No. 12553 Zambezi Road, Lusaka. PeeringDB lists the facility as NetOne Data Lusaka with networks present (read 21 September 2026) and describes it as multi-tenant and carrier-neutral. No Uptime Institute award for NetOne was found.

facilities.name: MTN Business Zambia Lusaka Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Listed by OCOLO as an MTN Business colocation site on Danny Pule Road, Lusaka, with no specifications. MTN Zambia is an MTN Group subsidiary; its shareholding is not sourced here.

facilities.name: TelOne Mazowe Data Centre (Mazowe Earth Station)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: At the Mazowe Earth Station north of Harare. Opened with TelOne's Harare data centre in March 2017 under the National Broadband project, funded by a $98M China Exim Bank loan and built with Huawei (DCD, 2017). A US$1M extension commissioned in March 2022 added a fourth Performance Optimised Data Centre module, taking it from 14 to 34 racks and 300 kW of IT load (263Chat; TechnoMag); investment_usd is that extension only. TelOne names banks, telcos and government departments among its customers (TechnoMag, March 2022). At the Mazowe expansion launch TelOne's chairman said the new module lets customers including government departments take disaster recovery hosting there (TechnoMag, March 2022).

facilities.name: TelOne Bulawayo Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Commissioned 28 April 2022 in Bulawayo CBD with a customer experience centre at Hillside; 120 racks and 400 kVA, Tier III by design (not certified), the first data centre in Matabeleland (Techzim; Ecofin; TechnoMag). DCmag says it is mainly equipped by Huawei; 400 kVA is the power rating reported, not IT load. DCD and DCmag give the power as 400 kW, Techzim and Ecofin as 400 kVA; none says it is IT load.

facilities.name: Airtel Malawi Blantyre Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Opened in Blantyre in December 2013 with over US$1M invested, doubling Airtel Malawi's capacity to host its own ICT systems, with cloud services promised (DCD, 3 December 2013). investment_usd is 'over $1m' as reported. No later source on the site was found. Commissioned at Airtel's head offices in Limbe, Blantyre (Nyasa Times, November 2013). The 2025 presentation names Blantyre as the primary data centre and Lilongwe as disaster recovery; it does not say whether this is the 2013 build.

facilities.name: Paratus Swakopmund Cable Landing Station (Equiano)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Built by Paratus as landing party, with Telecom Namibia as infrastructure partner, under a February 2021 agreement with Google; the building was finished in June-September 2021, fit-out (power, cabinets, cages, security) in January 2022, and the cable landed on 1 July 2022 (ITWeb; Submarine Networks). The station is also a meeting point where operators collect and distribute capacity. DCD (2023) says Armada (NAM-001) acts as the landing station; ITWeb and Paratus place it in Swakopmund, and Armada is the Windhoek data centre it backhauls to. Paratus Namibia Holdings' 2025 integrated report puts the station on Erf 3560, Swakopmund, a 1,000 m2 plot, and gives the building's cost as N$29,691,662 excluding the internal fit-out; investment_usd converts that at about N$14.79 to the dollar, the 2021 average, when the building was put up. Paratus' factsheet (September 2025) gives a 500 m2 data centre on a 1,000 m2 yard, 31 racks of which 20 are for Equiano and Google, a dedicated Erongo Red substation, two 250 kVA generators, and operation from November 2021; it is unmanned.

facilities.name: BDIH Data Centre (Botswana Digital & Innovation Hub)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: In the Hub's building at Plot 69184, Block 8, Science and Technology Park, Gaborone: 80 racks, Tier III compliant by the Hub's own description (not certified), two power circuits, UPS and two generators, a meet-me room with BoFiNet, VBN and BTC connected; tenants bring their own servers and internet. Uptime Institute lists a 'Government Integrated Data Centre 1 (GIDC 1), Phase 1' for the Hub as client, which may be this facility. Separate from BoFiNet's Digital Delta Data Centre (BWA-002) on its own plot in the same park. No source found ties Uptime's GIDC 1 award, whose client is the Hub and whose award type is not shown, to this data centre, or gives its opening year.

facilities.name: Government of Lesotho Primary Data Centre (Ministry of Finance, Maseru)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Finance and Development Planning
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The government's primary data centre at the Ministry of Finance in Maseru, which the Mohale's Hoek site (LSO-003) backs up (Government of Lesotho, May 2018). In 2025 the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning awarded Mapota Technologies a three-year LSL 35.6M contract to replace end-of-life government data hosting equipment and build a public-sector business continuity framework under the World Bank's Public Sector Foundations project (P174171), which is the status source. MoFDP's terms of reference for the IFMIS upgrade (c. 2025) say the IFMIS servers bought in 2018 are still in operation, serving all ministries; it does not name the building, and no opening year was found.

facilities.name: Sonangol Corporate Data Centre (Luanda)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Inaugurated 25 February 2026 for Sonangol's 50th anniversary; consolidates data centres previously spread across its subsidiaries. 920 m2 is the building (administration, SOC, NOC, UPS and communications rooms); the data hall is 400 m2, 182 m2 in use (Angop, PTI). Site within Luanda not stated. Separate from MSTelcom's data centres (AGO-005 to AGO-007), a Sonangol subsidiary.

facilities.name: Ministry of Finance Data Centre (Ngaliema, Kinshasa)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Finance of the DRC
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 2 November 2023 on avenue Colonel Mon Pia, Ma Campagne, Ngaliema; billed as the first national data centre and the first of three planned for the finance ministry's 'maisons des finances'. Built by Huawei under a December 2017 contract amended in 2020, with financing through cooperation with China. 54 servers, 1,278 TB of storage, two 480 kVA generators (Primature). Distinct from the government data centre in the Immeuble du Gouvernement, Gombe (COD-005). Financed by a USD 150 million China EXIM loan for the finance ministry's modernisation project, approved by Ordinance 20/130 of 31 July 2020 (AfricaNews RDC; Xinhua).

facilities.name: Lofoy HPC Data Centre (Université Nouveaux Horizons)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Inaugurated 27 June 2026 on the Université Nouveaux Horizons campus: two rooms, one holding 4 racks (30 servers) plus storage servers, with a control room (La Guardia, DecryptEco, RFI via Africain Times). Aimed at research and AI; the university plans to rent storage to banks, miners and public bodies. The university's own page names the supercomputer Lofoyi: 150 TFLOPS on servers linked by 100 Gbps InfiniBand, optimised for scientific computing, AI and big data; the new UNH data centre was inaugurated at the same ceremony (UNH, 27 June 2026). Accelerators are not named.

facilities.name: Airtel Gabon Data Centre (Libreville)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Directory listings (Inflect, DataCenterJournal) place Airtel's Libreville data centre at Rue Pecqueur, Libreville Business Square, offering cabinets, cages and connectivity; DCD (2025) lists Airtel Gabon among Libreville's existing data centres. Listings are undated.

facilities.name: Orange Cameroun Data Centre (Makepe, Douala)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
