facilities.note: Inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 31 May 2017 at Makepe, Douala V, in Orange Cameroun's 12,880 m2 complex; the data hall is 1,040 m2 (Campus Jeunes; DCD gives 1,000 m2 of data centre). Cost 16bn FCFA for the whole complex (TechAfrika). DCD calls it carrier-neutral with 99.98% uptime. Blue Sun DC lists it as 500+500 kW IT, Tier III+ design (2017); whether the second 500 kW was built is not reported. Orange Business Cameroun's page (read October 2026) describes it as Tier III+, inaugurated May 2017, built on three levels of 1,050 m² each, with 340 racks in two white rooms, two medium-voltage grid feeds from separate substations, two fibre entry points and 99.82% availability; the 1,050 m² levels are the building, not white space. A solar system at the Makepe complex went into production in November 2023, producing about 362 MWh a year and covering about 30% of the equipment's power demand (BFI, March 2025).

facilities.name: Orange Cameroun Data Centre (Yaoundé)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Blue Sun DC CEMAC lists a 200 kW Tier III+ design data centre for Orange in Yaoundé (2023), for which it was engineer (MOE). No other source; site and status unconfirmed.

facilities.name: MTN Cameroon DC1 (Yaoundé)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: MTN's colocation offer names DC1 at Yaoundé and DC2 at Douala. Blue Sun DC CEMAC lists a 420 kW Tier III certification project for MTN in Yaoundé (2022); MTN says its data centre holds Uptime Tier III design certification for 320 kW peak IT load (300 kW in the data hall), without naming the site. Uptime Institute's award register lists MTN Cameroon's 'Yaoundé DC', which ties the Tier III design certificate to this site; it_capacity_mw is the certified 320 kW.

facilities.name: MTN Cameroon DC2 (Douala)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: MTN's colocation offer names DC2 at Douala alongside DC1 at Yaoundé; Systalink (2026) lists MTN data centres in Douala and Yaoundé. No capacity or site details. Status kept Operational: MTN Cameroon's colocation price list, read September 2026, offers space at the Douala site.

facilities.name: Orange Centrafrique Data Centre (Sodiam, Bangui)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Orange Centrafrique's data centre, radio installations and network core at its main Sodiam site in Bangui were destroyed by fire on 6 June 2021, taking the whole network down (Digital Business Africa, RFI). Whether the data centre was rebuilt on the site is not reported. Orange restored all services on 30 June 2021, 23 days after the fire (Agence Ecofin), without saying whether a data centre was rebuilt at Sodiam.

facilities.name: Vodacom Mwanza Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Vodacom Tanzania's colocation privacy supplement (undated, read September 2026) lists Mwanza among the five places its colocation data centres are, and says its data centres are ISO 27001 certified (written 'ISO 2701'). No address, capacity or opening year published.

facilities.name: Vodacom Arusha Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Vodacom Tanzania's colocation privacy supplement (undated, read September 2026) lists Arusha among the five places its colocation data centres are, and says its data centres are ISO 27001 certified (written 'ISO 2701'). No address, capacity or opening year published.

facilities.name: Vodacom Mbeya Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Vodacom Tanzania's colocation privacy supplement (undated, read September 2026) lists Mbeya among the five places its colocation data centres are, and says its data centres are ISO 27001 certified (written 'ISO 2701'). No address, capacity or opening year published.

facilities.name: Nxtra by Airtel Dar es Salaam
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: DCD (December 2024) lists Dar es Salaam after Lagos and Nairobi among Nxtra's planned data centres; TechTrendsKE (April 2026) and edgeX (August 2026) repeat it. Nxtra's CEO said in July 2026 that the first builds are Nigeria, Kenya and the DRC. No site, capacity or date published; status as of August 2026.

facilities.name: Zanzibar National Data Centre (ZICTIA)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The Zanzibar Communication Corporation Act (No. 4 of 2023) charges ZICTIA with managing the Zanzibar National Data Center, defined as a data centre owned by the Government; ZICTIA sells colocation and virtual servers from it and has its head office at Mazizini. ZIBI (November 2025) reports an upgrade taking storage from 5 TB to 45 TB and also describes a US$75m Tier III centre of 200 racks and 2 MW without making clear whether that is this site or a planned one. Distinct from the Union ministry's planned Zanzibar national data centre (TZA-018). Correction: ZIBI lists the US$75m, 200-rack, 2 MW Tier III centre among ZICTIA's upcoming projects, so it is a planned facility, not this site. UN DESA (January 2013) reports President Shein launching an e-government centre at Mazizini built with China's ZTE among suppliers; The Citizen (August 2018) says a data centre for Zanzibar's hospitals had been completed at Mazizini. Neither says which date is this data centre's opening. Zanzibar's communications minister said on 2 October 2026 that more than TZS 53 billion is set aside for three ICT infrastructure projects, chiefly a data centre and public internet; he named no site, capacity or completion date.

facilities.name: Lumitel Bujumbura
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Lumitel's general manager says the company has built data centres in Burundi alongside its mobile and fibre networks (August 2026); AFRINIC registers Viettel Burundi address blocks for 'Data Center Service' in Bujumbura, where its head office is at 51 Boulevard de l'Uprona, Rohero. No site, capacity, services or opening year published. Lumitel's Stevie Awards entry (January 2025) lists a ServerCloud server-rental service among its ICT products; whether the data centres also sell colocation is not stated.

facilities.name: Guinea-Bissau National Data Centre (Alto Bandim)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: UNDP began building the national data centre in the Alto Bandim neighbourhood of Bissau in March 2026, due for completion in July 2026, in a project that also builds the new headquarters of ITMA and offices for the data-protection and cybersecurity agencies; funded by the Government of Japan, US$762,000 for the whole project (Conosaba do Porto, 14 March 2026, quoting UNDP). UNDP's 2025 annual report lists 'National Data Center construction launched'. The World Bank's digital economy diagnostic (2021) found no government data centre in the country. Completion not reported by September 2026. Mais Afrika (29 March 2024) gives EUR 1.93M from Japan for the ITMA headquarters building that will house the data centre; neither figure is for the data centre alone. Completion by the July 2026 target is not reported.

facilities.name: Orange Liberia Buchanan Tier III+ Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Orange Liberia said in July 2025 it is building a Tier III+ data centre in Buchanan, Grand Bassa County, to support cloud services, e-governance platforms and fintech with local data hosting (The Liberian Investigator, 23 July 2025, Liberia Tech Summit). MoPT's 2026 draft data governance policy mentions a Tier III+ facility under development in Buchanan. Buchanan is the planned landing site of Liberia's second subsea cable. Tier III+ is the design claim, not a certification; size, cost and date not stated. Orange's consolidation list (31 December 2024) gives the group a 72.50% interest in Orange Liberia Inc, as in Orange Côte d'Ivoire. Orange Liberia's CEO said in May 2025 that the Buchanan centre will complement the existing Monrovia data centre as a disaster-recovery site, will be open to hosting other companies' and institutions' data, and was expected to be inaugurated early in 2026 (Liberian Observer, 5 May 2025).

facilities.name: Central Bank of Liberia Main Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The African Development Fund granted US$3.9M in 2023 to upgrade CBL's main data centre and disaster-recovery site with its payment systems (DCD, March 2023; MFDP, May 2023); the project runs to December 2026 (Liberia Development Dashboard). Site and size not published. Distinct from the new CBL-owned data centre planned in the LIB-PSS building (LBR-006). An undated blog by George Fahnbulleh says CBL built its data centre in Virginia, Montserrado County, outside central Monrovia; not confirmed elsewhere. The Fahnbulleh post is dated 20 November 2013; it says CBL had already built its data centre in Virginia, with fibre extended there and triple power redundancy. The AfDB appraisal (March 2023) says CBL has two data centres, the main one at its Monrovia headquarters, at full capacity and unable to take the new national payment switch, and a disaster-recovery site about seven miles from the capital with room to grow; the upgrade component is costed at UA 689,646 (US$917,808). On 28 September 2026 CBL issued an international invitation for bids (IFB CBL/G/PS/2026/01) for the Data Centers Upgrade (Main and DR) under the AfDB-financed Liberia Payments Infrastructure and Systems Upgrade Project, with bids due on 28 October 2026 and a US$18,000 bid security.

facilities.name: Sierra Leone Ministry of Finance Data Centre
facilities.operator: Ministry of Finance (Sierra Leone), Directorate of Financial Management Systems and Technology (DFMST)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The NPPA inspected the Ministry of Finance data centre, which hosts the national e-Government Procurement platform, on 7 January 2026; the ministry's Director of ICT and Head of the Data Center described its cooling, racks and network; disaster recovery is not yet in place (Sierraloaded, 7 January 2026). Size not stated. The ministry's DFMST page (read October 2026) says the directorate, set up in 2022, operates a modern Tier III data centre housing MoF systems and co-locating several financial-sector institutions; Tier III is self-described, with no certification named.

facilities.name: BCRG Data Centre (Banque Centrale de la République de Guinée)
facilities.operator: Banque Centrale de la République de Guinée (BCRG)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: In January 2026 the BCRG sought a consultant (assistance à maîtrise d'ouvrage) for the interior fit-out and Tier III certification of its data centre, funded from its own resources under its 2025 budget (Yodalan, 12 January 2026). Size and site not stated; Tier III is the target, not a certification. Status per Africaguinée (11 April 2025): the BCRG budgeted a new power module and replacement UPS batteries for its Conakry data centre, and LED panels at two sites, so the January 2026 fit-out tender upgrades a running facility.

facilities.name: MTN Guinée Coléah Data Centre
facilities.operator: Areeba Guinée S.A. (formerly branded MTN Guinée)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: MTN Guinée showed journalists its new data centre at Coléah, Conakry, in November 2013, alongside its 3G+ launch (Africaguinee, 15 November 2013). Its current operator and status are not sourced. The State bought MTN Group's 75% of Areeba Guinée S.A. (trading as MTN Guinée) in December 2024 and took full ownership by decree on 11 December 2025 (Ecofin; Guinéenews). No current operator page or PeeringDB record shows the Coléah site, so status stays Unknown.

facilities.name: 21st Century Technologies Saka-Tinubu Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Listed on 21CTL's own site as its Saka-Tinubu data centre, Victoria Island: 'a large, multi-tenant facility with multiple carrier and utility feeds and strong electrical and mechanical redundancy' (September 2026). 1A Samuel Adedoyin Street is 21CTL's Victoria Island office (21CTL support-centres page); the data centre's own street address is not published, and the coordinates are approximate. 21CTL's site also lists Ikoyi, Apapa, Ikeja and Alanamu data centres.

facilities.name: Cloud Exchange Ikoyi Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: 17 Lugard Avenue, Ikoyi. Launched 4 October 2021 with Huawei as a modular prefabricated data centre, billed as Africa's first Uptime Tier IV prefabricated facility; the Uptime register shows a Tier IV Certification of Design Documents only. Cloud Exchange West Africa was previously Dimension Data Limited (Nigeria) (Uptime). IXPN lists it as a Lagos PoP (Lineserve, July 2026, which also lists the site as live). A Cummins West Africa case study (May 2025) says it supplied two diesel generators and the switching that combines them with gas IPP supply and the grid, which it credits for the Tier IV certification; it does not say which certification.

facilities.name: AWS Local Zone Lagos
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Launched 26 January 2023 as an AWS Local Zones location in Lagos, extending an AWS Region for low-latency and in-country workloads; Amazon GameLift added the Nigeria Local Zone in July 2024. AWS does not name the host data centre. The AWS Direct Connect location in Lagos (Rack Centre, May 2023) is a separate service. AWS's Local Zones list confirms the zone (af-south-1-los-1a, parent Region af-south-1); AWS names no host building, and a search found none.

facilities.name: Airtel Nigeria Lekki Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Launched for commercial use on 12 April 2022 in Lekki, Lagos: 200 racks, hosting and cloud services for business and government, rated TIA-942 Rated 3 by EPI (DCD corrected an earlier 'Tier 3'). Status rests on the 2022 launch reports. Separate from the 38MW Nxtra facility under construction at Eko Atlantic (NGA-021). Owner Airtel Networks Limited; address 2-6 Dr. Muiz Banire Street, Lekki Phase 1 (TIA register). Its TIA-942-B Design Rated 3 certificate expired on 27 January 2023. Status set to Unknown: nothing after 2022 confirms operation. EPI's ANSI/TIA-942-B Rated 3 design certificate (TIA942NG220128001) was dated 28 January 2022 and ran to 27 January 2023 (TIA Online).

facilities.name: GTBank DC01
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: GTBank's stand-alone data centre, built with Resourcery Plc to meet the CBN requirement that banks' data centres satisfy Uptime Tier III; Tier III Certification of Design Documents (August 2019), no constructed-facility certificate on the register. Status rests on the 2019 reports and Lineserve (July 2026), which lists it as a private enterprise site.

facilities.name: LAGIS ABAT-3 Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Housed in the new LAGIS office at Alausa, Ikeja; commissioned 8 April 2026 by President Tinubu (represented by Senate President Akpabio) to host and protect the state's digitised land records (status as of that date). Hosts Lagos State land and geospatial data (LAGIS). Uptime separately lists a 'Lagos State Data Centre' (client Lagos State Government, Tier III design documents) with no address; a September 2026 search did not establish whether it is this facility.

facilities.name: 24DNL Modular Data Centre, Duport Energy Park
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Modular data centre in the Duport Energy Park at Egbokor, Orhionmwon LGA, Edo State (the nearest city is Benin City), part of phase one of the FCMB-financed park of Duport Midstream Company alongside a modular refinery, gas processing and a power plant; phase one was due on stream in March 2022. Uptime lists it with a Tier IV Certification of Design Documents only. No source confirms the data centre entered service. Huawei and 24DNL signed a partnership in November 2020 under which 24DNL would build, install and commission the data centre for the park (ThisDay). A September 2026 search found no report that it entered service and no disclosure of 24DNL's owners.

facilities.name: OADC Bree Street (CPT3)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Formerly Internet Solutions (NTT DATA) Cape Town, 34 Bree Street, The Terraces; NTT's page described five colocation halls built to TIA-942 Tier III principles. OADC bought it with six other NTT sites (completed 31 December 2025) and NTT leases it back. OADC's page gives 1,200 m² and Tier III design; whether that is white space is not stated. An established CINX site (15 networks, August 2026). RSAWEB DC2 (ZAF-046) is in the same building. Internet Solutions was already running an International Data Centre in Cape Town when it upgraded the power room in August 2007 (ITWeb); no source gives the opening year.

facilities.name: NTT Bellville Data Centre (Sanlam head office)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Underground in Sanlam's Bellville head office, 'purpose-built and shared with Sanlam' (NTT); five data halls to TIA-942 Tier III principles, housing financial-services clients. Rackzar lists 2 MW, not stated as IT load. Not among the seven sites NTT sold to OADC (its one Cape Town site in that deal was Bree Street). NTT's page is undated. No 2025-26 source confirms the site is running or names its owner; OADC's own pages list no Bellville facility.

facilities.name: xneelo Samrand 2
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Second xneelo data centre in Samrand, construction started February 2026, due October 2026; modelled on the first Samrand facility (ZAF-036). Size and cost not disclosed (DCD, 3 February 2026).

facilities.name: Vantage JNB12 (Johannesburg I - Waterfall City)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Second building on Vantage's Johannesburg I campus in Waterfall City (JNB11 is ZAF-023). Attacq reported the development complete in 2026, supporting an initial 12 MW electrical load, ramping to 16 MW; 12 MW is total load, not IT load. 10,363 m² two-storey building with four data halls (DCD, March 2025). Vantage leases the shell from the Attacq joint venture for 20 years; no source discloses who owns the fit-out. Attacq values its share of the property at R589M (2026).

facilities.name: Microsoft Centurion Data Centre Campus (Kosmosdal)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Microsoft advertised its intention to build a data centre campus in Kosmosdal, Centurion, in February 2024, 'still in the early phases of development'; no size or timeline given. A March 2026 commentary calls it under construction, which no primary source confirms. Microsoft's investment figures sit on ZAF-041. Microsoft's April 2026 breakdown of its R5.4bn commitment includes land for future campuses; no source reports construction at Kosmosdal or ties it to Cavaleros' Cosmas Data City (ZAF-049), which Baxtel places about 1 km away.

facilities.name: Oracle Cloud Johannesburg Region (af-johannesburg-1)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Oracle's first African cloud region, available 8 January 2022 (release notes) and announced 19 January 2022; one availability domain. Oracle declined to disclose the data centre's location or size (ITWeb). FastConnect partners at launch: Colt, Telia, Equinix, Megaport.

facilities.name: SITA Numerus Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: SITA's second main data centre, in its Numerus building in Pretoria, a National Key Point (ITWeb, 2015). IBM South Africa won a 2022 contract to replace its mainframes; SITA's 2023 BMC tender covers the Numerus and Centurion data centres. Address and capacity not published. A briefing to Parliament's communications committee names Centurion (primary) and Beta (secondary) as SITA's two main data centres and does not mention Numerus.

facilities.name: SARS Brooklyn Data Centre (Le Hae la SARS)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: One of SARS's two data centres (Brooklyn and Alberton) named in its 2025 generator-maintenance tender (RFP 20/2025A), at the Le Hae la SARS campus, 299 Bronkhorst Street, Nieuw Muckleneuk; three Mitsubishi generators of 1,850 kVA each (2010 and 2012). Capacity not published.

facilities.name: SARS Alberton Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: SARS's second data centre, at its Alberton campus, named in its 2025 generator-maintenance tender (RFP 20/2025A); two MTU generators of 1,600 kVA each (2013). Capacity and address not published.

facilities.name: MTN Doornfontein Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: MTN's own data centre in Doornfontein, upgraded for reliability, uptime and white space by AOS Consulting Engineers (project page, 2022). MTN told ITWeb in October 2025 it is closing third-party sites (Gallo Manor, Great Westerford) and consolidating into its own and partner facilities. The Doornfontein Switch, 31 Height Street, is a site in scope of MTN's ISO 27001:2022 certificate (SABS, re-certified 22 October 2025 after a March 2025 audit, expires 12 October 2028), which is what the status rests on.

facilities.name: INWI Tangier Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: inwi's cloud and data centre director listed Tangier among inwi's operational data centres in June 2023 (Aujourd'hui le Maroc); Datacenters.com lists an inwi Tangier Data Center. Address, size and certification not public. inwi staff announced the new Meknes, Tangier and Agadir data centres in June 2022 (LinkedIn); inwi had six data centres by June 2023 (LesEco).

facilities.name: INWI Oujda Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: inwi's cloud and data centre director listed Oujda among inwi's operational data centres in June 2023 (Aujourd'hui le Maroc); Datacenters.com lists an inwi Oujda Data Center. Address, size and certification not public. In June 2022 inwi staff listed Oujda among data centres due in the coming months (LinkedIn); it was operating by June 2023, so it opened between those dates.

facilities.name: INWI Meknes Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: inwi's cloud and data centre director listed Meknes among inwi's operational data centres in June 2023 (Aujourd'hui le Maroc); Datacenters.com lists an inwi Meknes Data Center. Address, size and certification not public. inwi staff announced the new Meknes, Tangier and Agadir data centres in June 2022 (LinkedIn); inwi had six data centres by June 2023 (LesEco).

facilities.name: INWI Agadir Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: inwi's cloud and data centre director listed Agadir among inwi's operational data centres in June 2023 (Aujourd'hui le Maroc); Datacenters.com lists an inwi Agadir Data Center. Address, size and certification not public. inwi staff announced the new Meknes, Tangier and Agadir data centres in June 2022 (LinkedIn); inwi had six data centres by June 2023 (LesEco).

facilities.name: Ministry of Economy and Finance Primary Data Center (MEF/DC1)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The ministry's primary data centre, hosting most of its information systems; Uptime audited it in Q4 2024 and certified it Tier III Constructed Facility in February 2025, the first in Moroccan public administration (Le Matin, La Vie Eco). The ministry set up the data centre in 2012 and obtained Uptime Tier III Design certification at the end of 2021 (ministry communiqué, January 2022).

facilities.name: ESI National Data Centre (Centre national des données)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The higher-education minister inspected the national data centre run by ESI-Alger on 21 July 2025 while checking preparations for the 2025 university pre-registrations (APS); status as of that visit. No capacity or certification published.

facilities.name: ENSIA AI Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: A data centre for AI applications at the National Higher School of Artificial Intelligence, with NVIDIA H100, L40S and A40 GPUs and an open-source software stack; the minister visited it on 29 July 2025 (MESRS). No capacity published. The centre is at the Abdelhafid-Ihaddaden science and technology hub, Sidi Abdellah (Algiers), and was inaugurated in July 2025 (L'Express DZ, Middle East AI News).

facilities.name: CNI National Backup Centre (Bizerte)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: The state's recovery site for critical government applications, begun in 2006 with World Bank support and replicating asynchronously from CNI's Tunis data centre (TUN-005); CNI tendered generator maintenance and fire-protection works at the Bizerte backup centre in 2023-2024 (cni.tn). Directinfo (February 2013) says the centre, at Errimel (Menzel Jemil, Bizerte), was created from 2008 with US$2.2 million of World Bank co-financing and TND 3 million from the Fonds de développement des communications; its architectural design was tendered in July 2008. Opening year not published. The project began with a call for consultants in September 2004, under a World Bank ICT-sector loan, with CNI as executing agency (WMC).

facilities.name: Orange Tunisie Charguia Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Orange Tunisie's historic data centre at Charguia, Tunis; the Kalaa Kebira site (TUN-004), opened May 2025, gives it geographic redundancy in a two-data-centre architecture (OnTech, Challenges, May 2025). Size and year not published. Telec Tunisie refitted the electrical installations of Orange Tunisie's Charguia site in 2017; Charguia is in Greater Tunis (Ariana governorate).

facilities.name: Tunisie Telecom Kasbah Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Opened September 2010 in the Kasbah administrative quarter: a 280 sqm server room (white space) with 92 racks for ministries, administrations, banks and firms (Kapitalis, WMC, Leaders). Tunisie Telecom's 2018 ITU presentation, cited on TUN-002, lists Kasbah as the secondary site behind Carthage; status rests on that. A September 2026 search found no mention of the Kasbah site after 2018; Tunisie Telecom's 2025 material names only its Carthage data centre, so status is Unknown. An ITU report (2020) still lists Kasba as Tunisie Telecom's secondary data centre, about 20 km from Carthage, hosting its SaaS platform, with 1 Gbit/s fibre links to the backbone.

facilities.name: Tunisie Telecom Kairouan Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Planned in 2013 as Tunisie Telecom's backup data centre and being finalised in July 2017 (THD, Tekiano); the 2018 ITU presentation cited on TUN-002 names Kairouan as the disaster-recovery site behind Carthage. A September 2026 search found no mention of the Kairouan site after 2018 and no opening date; status is Unknown. An ITU report (2020) describes Kairouan as recently established and in use for disaster recovery, about 160 km from Carthage, with 10 Gbit/s fibre links to the backbone; that is the latest source to say it runs.

facilities.name: Eurafric Information DC Bouskoura (BSK)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Bank of Africa BMCE Group's data centre at Bouskoura, run by its IT arm Eurafric Information; Tier III constructed per ICTworks' reading of the Uptime register (August 2026). Size and year not published. Eurafric Information, created in October 2008, is Bank of Africa's IT subsidiary, a partnership of Bank of Africa, RMA and Crédit Mutuel Alliance Fédérale's Euro-Information; O Capital Group reports owning 51% of it.

facilities.name: Banque Centrale Populaire Data Center Berrechid
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Groupe Banque Populaire's data centre at Berrechid, registered by Uptime as Phases 1 and 2; Tier III constructed per ICTworks' reading of the register (August 2026). Size and year not published.

facilities.name: Crédit Agricole du Maroc Rabat Data Center
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Crédit Agricole du Maroc's data centre in Rabat; Tier III constructed per ICTworks' reading of the Uptime register (August 2026). Size and year not published.

facilities.name: Maroclear CSD Morocco DC1
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Data centre of Maroclear, Morocco's central securities depository, in Casablanca; Tier III constructed per ICTworks' reading of the Uptime register (August 2026). Size and year not published.

facilities.name: Finacards Data Center 01
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Data centre of Finacards, a card supplier and personaliser for financial, government and private clients, at Bouskoura; Tier III constructed per ICTworks' reading of the Uptime register (August 2026). Size and year not published. La Vie Eco (February 2014) reports BMCE Bank's wholly owned Docuprint taking over Finatech's card business Finacard, including its Bouskoura centre; whether Finacards SA is still in Bank of Africa's group is not confirmed.

facilities.name: STEG Sfax Data Center
facilities.operator: Société Tunisienne de l'Electricité et du Gaz (STEG)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: STEG, the Tunisian electricity and gas company, tendered an upgrade of the electrical installations of its Sfax data centre in July 2026 (bid 20260701543, closing 2 September 2026); status rests on that tender. No size, year or certification published.

facilities.name: KNUST Data Centre (Kumasi)
facilities.operator: KNUST Network Operations and Infrastructure Division (NOID)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: KNUST's NOID reports its new Tier-3 enterprise data centre about 95% complete in January 2026, with primary infrastructure operational and final cooling, UPS and solar-inverter (60 to 90 kW) works outstanding; it describes a 250+ m² facility built to ANSI/TIA Tier III with N+1 redundancy and 22+ Gbps backbone capacity. Tier III is the university's own description, not a certification.

facilities.name: MTN Côte d'Ivoire Technology Center Data Centre (Zone 4)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Abidjan.net (June 2014) says MTN's Yopougon data centre 'is added to the data centre of the Technology Center, opened in 2011 in Zone 4'. No later source gives its status. MTN Côte d'Ivoire's 2024 interconnection catalogue offers colocation at its Marcory Technology Centre ('TC Marcory'), Bingerville, Yopougon and Yamoussoukro data centres; Zone 4 lies in Marcory, so this row is taken to be TC Marcory (read September 2026).

facilities.name: MTN Abidjan Data Centre (Bd François Mitterrand)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: OCOLO and DataCenterMap list an MTN Abidjan colocation site on Bd François Mitterrand, which runs through Cocody; in June 2014 MTN announced a third data centre at Cocody Riviera for the second half of 2014, which this may be. Not the Yopougon eCentre (CIV-005). The third data centre MTN announced for Cocody Riviera in June 2014 was built instead at Bingerville, east of Abidjan, as a Flexenclosure eCentre due in service in October 2014 (Jeune Afrique, September 2014); Bd François Mitterrand runs from Cocody to Bingerville, so the directory listing is taken to be that site. MTN's 2024 interconnection catalogue offers colocation at Bingerville (read September 2026).

facilities.name: Côte d'Ivoire E-Government Data Centre (Grand-Bassam)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Built by Huawei under the E-Government Project, financed by a China Eximbank RMB 240m (FCFA 15bn) government concessional loan signed January 2008 and disbursed by December 2013; construction completed 9 November 2012 (AidData). China Daily (November 2012) reports the launch and a $30m cost connected to 52 ministry websites; Digital Mag (July 2026) lists it among the country's data centres at FCFA 16bn. Status rests on that 2026 listing. Whether SNDI (CIV-006) runs it is not stated. Investment is the $30m project cost reported at launch (China Daily, AITN, November 2012); Digital Mag's FCFA 16bn is about $31m at 2012 rates, and the RMB 240m China Eximbank loan about $35m at 2008 rates. Which agency runs it is not published. An African Development Bank appraisal (June 2023) counts one government data centre at VITIB Grand-Bassam as not functional, with mould in its walls; it does not say whether that is this centre or VITIB's own (CIV-014). Status still rests on the 2026 listing. The PARAE project document (June 2023, reported by Sika Finance in September 2026) says the fifth state data centre, in the Grand-Bassam free zone, was reportedly at a complete standstill; it does not name it, so whether that is this centre or VITIB's (CIV-014) is not stated.

facilities.name: VITIB Data Centre (Grand-Bassam)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Donated to VITIB by MTN (FCFA 275m) and inaugurated 16 December 2011 in the Grand-Bassam free zone (Abidjan.net). Digital Mag (July 2026) lists it among the public data centres, offering public entities and approved companies secure colocation. Status rests on that 2026 source. VITIB SA, created in 2006 with FCFA 3bn of capital, has Ivorian and foreign shareholders including the Ivorian state, Prestige Télécom, Petro CI, SOTRA and CI Télécom; no split is published (Observatoire Europe-Afrique 2030 fiche, 2016). The 2016 free-zone fiche describes the data centre as hosting equipment and data for companies with regulated power, a 1,050 kVA generator, three fibre connections, an ISP platform, VSAT internet backup, biometric access and video surveillance. An African Development Bank appraisal (June 2023) counts one government data centre at VITIB Grand-Bassam as not functional, with mould in its walls; it does not say whether that is this centre or the e-government centre (CIV-013). Status still rests on the 2026 listing.

facilities.name: Presidency of the Republic Data Centre (Côte d'Ivoire)
facilities.operator: Presidency of the Republic of Côte d'Ivoire
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Digital Mag (July 2026) lists the Presidency's data centre among the public data centres the state relies on pending the national data centre (CIV-007), dedicated to the communications and strategic data of the Republic's institutions. No size, date or address is given.

facilities.name: Kaydan Digital Data Centre Park (VITIB Grand-Bassam)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: A 5,000 m² park at VITIB for up to 40 to 45 co-located modular Tier 3 mini data centres (18 m² concrete modules, 2 to 4 IT racks each), with dual CIE feeds, two generators and 48 hours of fuel (Digital Mag, December 2024 and July 2026). Tier 3 is the owner's description. Kaydan Groupe is the Ivorian group led by its founder Alain Kouadio (Forbes Afrique, December 2023); its registration is not published.

facilities.name: DataConnect Tier III Data Centre (Côte d'Ivoire)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Dataconnect says it has its own Tier III data centre, PCI-DSS certified, with ISO 27001:2022 renewed by PECB across its Ivorian services in September 2025 (allAfrica, La Diplomatique d'Abidjan); its site advertises 2N power and cooling, two telecom rooms and 99.982% availability. Tier III is self-described. The site's address is not given; the company is based at Cocody Angré and also has an office at Grand-Bassam. PeeringDB lists a DATACONNECT COTE D'IVOIRE facility in Abidjan, with no networks (read September 2026). New Digital Africa was incubated inside the NSIA group before Ange Kacou Diagou took it over in 2020; in November 2022 it said it was finalising the entry of a strategic and financial partner (Africa Business+). Its shareholders are not published.

facilities.name: Ministry of Budget Shared Backup Data Centre (Yamoussoukro)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Budget and State Portfolio
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Housed at the Regional Tax Directorate in Yamoussoukro; foundation stone 23 September 2020, inaugurated 26 July 2021 as the shared backup site replicating the ministry's directorates' data outside Abidjan. Built by a telecom equipment supplier 'with Huawei's technological support' (Abidjan.net, July 2021).

facilities.name: Orange Côte d'Ivoire Assabou Data Centre (Yamoussoukro)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Orange Côte d'Ivoire signed 15-year contracts with SolarX (March 2023) to solarise this data centre at Assabou, Yamoussoukro, covering about half its daytime consumption, part of about 1 MWp across two sites (DCD, pv magazine). Not the GOS data centre at Grand-Bassam (CIV-004). Status rests on those 2023 sources. Orange Côte d'Ivoire's 2024 integrated report says two major data centres, in Côte d'Ivoire and Burkina Faso, were solarised in 2024.

facilities.name: Douanes BdM Datacenter (Dakar)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Uptime Institute's award register lists 'Douanes, BdM Datacenter', Dakar, Senegal, for the Direction Générale des Douanes, with Tier III Certification of Design Documents and of Constructed Facility; the award dates are not shown. Status rests on the Constructed Facility award: the building exists, but no dated source gives its current use. Uptime's register names the design award 'Bloc Des Madeleine' (Dakar) and dates the Constructed Facility award 29 September 2022; its client page links to the French customs website, which appears to be a register error.

facilities.name: Sénégal Connect Park Data Centre (Diamniadio)
facilities.operator: Ministry of Communication, Telecommunications and Digital Affairs (project owner; operating concession not settled)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: A Tier 3 data centre is part of the 12.5 ha Parc des Technologies Numériques (Sénégal Connect Park) at Diamniadio, whose works restarted in November 2025 with delivery promised before March 2026 (We Are Tech, Sans Limite); in May 2026 the Prime Minister put the park at 95% physical completion, held up by financing and contract blockages on a FCFA 74.5bn budget (Ocean's News). Tier 3 is the design target.

facilities.name: Orange Burkina Faso Balkuy Data Centre
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Orange's data centre at Balkuy, Ouagadougou, is to take 37% of its daytime power from a SolarX solar plant under a 15-year contract signed with Orange Côte d'Ivoire in March 2023 (DCD, pv magazine, The Electricity Hub). Status rests on those 2023 sources. Orange Burkina Faso is a subsidiary of Orange Côte d'Ivoire, which signed the SolarX contract; Orange CI's 2024 integrated report says the Burkina Faso data centre was solarised in 2024.

facilities.name: IPSyS Telecom Datacenter (Ouagadougou)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Listed by Data Center Platform and Inflect at Avenue Kwame N'Krumah, Koulouba, Ouagadougou; Inflect gives 0.5 MW of power. Directory listings only; no dated source gives its status.

facilities.name: Alink Telecom Ouagadougou Datacenter
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Data Center Platform lists two Alink Telecom data centres, in Cotonou (BEN-001) and Ouagadougou; a 2026 market survey describes the Ouagadougou one as a colocation data centre for operators and large companies. Directory listings only.

facilities.name: Comsys Porto Data Centre (Tema)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Uptime Institute awarded Comsys (GH) Limited Tier III Certification of Design Documents for its Porto Data Centre in Tema; the award foil is dated 2 October 2025 and expires 2027, so the facility was at design stage then. Comsys already sells colocation from an existing data centre (comsysghana.com), whose site is not given. Comsys was founded in 1998 by Jonathan Lamptey and partners (Graphic Online, March 2024); the UK register of overseas entities (May 2026) names Jonathan and Funmi Lamptey of Accra as beneficial owners. No report of construction at Porto has been found, so the status rests on the October 2025 design award.

facilities.name: GNPC RATC Data Centre (Accra)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Uptime Institute lists GNPC's 'RATC Data Centre', Accra, with Tier III Certification of Design Documents. GNPC describes its Research and Technology Centre (RATC) as set up to manage the data from its operations, and its CEO has proposed selling RATC capacity to the oil, gas and mining sectors. No source gives the facility's status or date. Reported newly built in September 2020 (B&FT, Modern Ghana), after GNPC sought approval in 2019 for $25m to redevelop its laboratory and data centre; GNPC's CEO toured the working RATC data hub in February 2025. GNPC is the national oil company established by PNDC Law 64 (1983). Status rests on the February 2025 visit. In April 2019 GNPC sought parliamentary approval for US$25M to redevelop its laboratory and data centre as the Research and Technology (RAT) Centre, a repository for its exploration and production data (Ghanaian Times via Ghana Talks Business); a budget request covering the laboratory too, so not recorded as the investment.

facilities.name: NITA Ghana E-Gov Cloud Data Center (Kumasi)
facilities.source_url_scope: Directory edition, not an independently reviewed facility source
facilities.note: Uptime Institute lists NITA's 'Ghana E-Gov Cloud Data Center', Kumasi, with Tier II Certification of Design Documents, beside NITA's Accra primary (GHA-005). GHA-005's comments record a secondary replica at KNUST, Kumasi, which this probably is; it is not KNUST's own data centre. NITA's national data centre launched in January 2016 with a secondary centre on the KNUST campus, Kumasi, run by NITA with Alcatel-Lucent and Huawei (Graphic Online); whether Uptime's Tier II-designed 'E-Gov Cloud' site is that centre, and its current status, are not reported. The June 2026 World Bank-financed tender names Kumasi as NITA's secondary data centre, running for 10 years and due for refresh; it describes a containerised all-in-one facility of 42 cabinets (32 AC, 10 DC), a 300 kVA N+1 modular UPS, 100 kW chillers in 3+1 and two 450 kVA generators, following the Accra description (the section heading is cut in the record); its Huawei network equipment is at end of support. rows.name: South Africa
rows.wage_basis: Monthly equivalent of hourly rate using country-specific assumed hours
rows.wage_note: PRIMARY GAZETTE. National Minimum Wage Act 9 of 2018 (as amended): R30.23 per ORDINARY HOUR worked with effect from 1 March 2026 (Government Gazette No. 54075 of 3 February 2026, Notice 7083, substituting clause 1 of Schedule 1 as previously set by Gazette No. 52053 of 4 February 2025 at R28.79). Farm workers and domestic workers also R30.23/h; Expanded Public Works Programme workers R16.62/h. The statute sets an HOURLY rate, not a monthly one, so monthly_minimum_wage is left BLANK; hourly_derived carries the statute's own hourly rate (30.23) rather than a computed value. assumed_monthly_hours = 45 x 52 / 12 = 195.0, from the BCEA s.9 maximum ordinary hours of 45 per week; an indicative month at 195 h would be about R5,894.85, which is NOT a statutory monthly minimum. The gov.za PDF URL is the official gazette file (direct download returned an error from this environment; the gazette number, notice number, rate and date are corroborated by CRS, Global Business and Labour Guide summaries of the same gazette).

rows.name: Morocco
rows.wage_basis: Monthly equivalent of hourly rate using country-specific assumed hours
rows.wage_note: Decret n 2.25.983 of 29 December 2025, published in Bulletin Officiel no. 7469, sets the legal hourly minimum wage (SMIG) for NON-AGRICULTURAL activities at 17.92 MAD per HOUR with effect from 1 January 2026 (up from 17.10 MAD since January 2025; the second tranche of the 29 April 2024 tripartite agreement, which also covered CGEM and COMADER). Article 1 of the decree (Arabic text read): from 1 January 2026 the hourly minimum is fixed at 17.92 dirhams. The statute sets an HOURLY rate, so monthly_minimum_wage is left BLANK and hourly_derived carries the decree's own hourly figure. SMAG (agriculture) is set on a DAILY basis: 97.44 MAD/day. assumed_monthly_hours = 44 x 52 / 12 = 190.67, from the Moroccan Labour Code legal working week of 44 hours (2,288 h/year); an indicative gross month would be about 3,416.9 MAD at 190.67 h (Moroccan commentary commonly quotes about 3,422 MAD using 191 h/month) - neither is a statutory monthly figure. CAVEAT: mtfp.gov.ma did not resolve (DNS) and sgg.gov.ma served no usable bulletin page from this environment, so the decree text was read from a legal portal reproducing the Bulletin Officiel text, corroborated by Biladi, Medias24 and Upsilon Consulting.

rows.name: Kenya
rows.wage_note: PRIMARY GAZETTE. Legal Notice No. 108 of 2026 substitutes the Schedule to the Regulation of Wages (General) Order and is deemed to have come into operation on 1 May 2026. Basic minimum MONTHLY wage for a general labourer (cleaner, sweeper, gardener, children's ayah, house servant, day watchman, messenger) in Nairobi, Mombasa, Kisumu, Nakuru and Eldoret cities = KSh 18,047.40 per month, EXCLUSIVE of housing allowance. Lower regional rates: KSh 16,650.95 (former municipalities and town councils of Mavoko, Ruiru, Limuru) and KSh 9,628.07 (all other areas). An earlier publication of the same order (Legal Notice No. 95 of 2026, Kenya Gazette Supplement No. 128, 29 May 2026) carries the same effective date and the same city rate but shows 9,268.07 for 'all other areas' vs 9,628.07 in LN 108 - an apparent discrepancy in the source. The Order also publishes statutory DAILY (KSh 868.44) and HOURLY (KSh 161.34) rates for the same occupation, stated in the schedule as INCLUSIVE of housing allowance; these do not reconcile with the basic monthly figure on any single hours convention (flagged as a source inconsistency, not converted). assumed_monthly_hours uses the 45 h/week full-time norm for Kenyan day work: 45 x 52 / 12 = 195.0. Sector-specific orders also exist (e.g. Regulation of Wages (Agricultural Industry) (Amendment) Order 2026, Legal Notice No. 96 of 2026).

rows.name: Egypt
rows.wage_note: OFFICIAL government source (State Information Service). The National Council of Wages raised the private-sector minimum wage to EGP 7,000 per MONTH, effective 1 March 2025 (previously EGP 6,000 from April/May 2024; sixth increase in three years). The same decision set, for the first time, a minimum HOURLY wage for part-time workers of EGP 28 per hour, and an annual periodic raise of at least 3% of the social-insurance wage (floor EGP 250/month). Separate public-sector/state floor: EGP 8,000/month announced 1 April 2026 and effective July 2026 - that increase applies to state and public-sector employees, NOT the private-sector floor, which was still EGP 7,000 as of September 2026. assumed_monthly_hours: Egyptian Labour Law 12/2003 sets a 48-hour week, 48 x 52 / 12 = 208.0.

rows.name: Cote d'Ivoire
rows.wage_note: Decret n 2022-986 du 21 decembre 2022 portant revalorisation du SMIG raised the monthly SMIG (industry, commerce and services) from 60,000 to 75,000 FCFA per MONTH, effective 1 January 2023. Monthly is the statutory unit of the Ivorian SMIG, so no conversion was needed. assumed_monthly_hours = 40 x 52 / 12 = 173.33, from the Ivorian Code du travail legal working week of 40 hours. A separate agricultural minimum (SMAG) applies to farm work; the commonly circulated claim that the same decree set the SMAG at 39,960 FCFA/month is NOT substantiated by the decree, which has only three articles (Art. 1 fixes the SMIG at 75,000 from 1 January 2023; Art. 2 repeals contrary provisions, superseding Decret n 2013-791 du 20 novembre 2013; Art. 3 charges the Minister of Employment with execution) - no SMAG figure recorded. CAVEAT: the Journal Officiel is behind the SGG paywall (sgg.gouv.ci/jo.php) and is not freely published; the value is corroborated by the government spokesman's Conseil des ministres statement of 21 December 2022 (abidjan.net, pressecotedivoire, CCIL-CI) and by the CNPS 'Communique a l'attention des employeurs' of 11 January 2023.

rows.name: Senegal
rows.wage_basis: Monthly equivalent of hourly rate using country-specific assumed hours
rows.wage_note: Decret n 2023-1710 du 07 aout 2023. Article 1: the hourly SMIG for workers on the 40-hour legal week is fixed at 370.526 FCFA. Article 2: the hourly SMAG (agricultural undertakings) is 236.865 FCFA. Article 6: the provisions take effect from 1 July 2023. It abrogates Decret n 2019-103 du 16 janvier 2019. The statute sets an HOURLY rate, so monthly_minimum_wage is left BLANK and hourly_derived carries the decree's own hourly figure. assumed_monthly_hours = 40 x 52 / 12 = 173.33, the 40-hour legal week being specified in the decree itself. Indicative monthly = 370.526 x 173.33 = about 64,224.5 FCFA; consistent with this, the ministerial arrete of 25 April 2025 on domestic workers sets category 1 at 64,223 FCFA/month. CAVEAT: the Journal Officiel is not freely accessible online; the decree text was read from a verbatim news reproduction, corroborated by WageIndicator (which cites Decret 2023-1710 revising the SMIG for the 40-hour week) and Financial Afrik ('Le Senegal augmente son SMIG de 11%'). Beware of widely circulated figures of about 52,500 FCFA/month, which correspond to Togo's SMIG, not Senegal's.

rows.name: Nigeria
rows.wage_note: National Minimum Wage (Amendment) Act 2024 raises the national minimum wage from NGN 30,000 to NGN 70,000 per MONTH (monthly is the statute's own unit). Act assented 29 July 2024 but the new rate is stated to take effect from 1 May 2024 (retroactive; employers owed the May-July 2024 difference). Review period shortened from 5 to 3 years. Working week: the Labour Act (Cap. L1) s.13 does NOT fix a universal weekly hour limit (normal hours are fixed by mutual agreement, collective bargaining or an industrial wages board); 40 h/week is the conventional full-time assumption (WageIndicator/Mywage.ng cite the 1981 law using 40 h), giving 40 x 52 / 12 = 173.33 h/month. CAVEAT: no free official gazette copy of the Act was located (nigerianlawguru / NSIWC sites not reachable); the NGN 70,000 figure and 1 May 2024 effective date come from a law-firm reproduction of the Act and multiple independent reports.

rows.name: Ghana
rows.wage_note: The statutory form is a DAILY rate: the National Tripartite Committee, acting under s.113(1)(a) of the Labour Act 2003 (Act 651), set the 2026 National Daily Minimum Wage at GH 21.77 per day, effective 1 January 2026 (2025: GH 19.97; +9%). monthly_minimum_wage = GH 587.79 = 21.77 x 27 working days, using the NTC's own 27-working-day month convention (the NTC summary of the determination gives GH 587.8 for 27 working days; 2025 equivalent GH 539.19); it is a body-set conversion, not an independent estimate. assumed_monthly_hours = 27 days x 8 h = 216 (Labour Act 2003 s.33: maximum 8 h/day, 40 h/week). The NTC also recommended that the 2026 NDMW be tax-exempt. CAVEAT: no official NTC / Ministry of Employment and Labour Relations web source was reachable (mlgpp.gov.gh did not resolve, ghana.gov.gh returned no wage page); rate confirmed by multiple Ghanaian outlets reporting the NTC communique. Review 11 November 2026: announced 2027/2028 wage changes are future rates, excluded from the 2026 benchmark.
